-def prepare_multipart(fields):
+def set_multipart_encoding(encoding):
+    """Takes a string specifying the encoding type for multipart data and
+    returns a reference to the corresponding function from the
+    ``email.encoders`` library.
+
+    :arg encoding: str
+    :returns: encoder function from ``email.encoders``
+    :raises ValueError: if the specified encoding is not supported
+    """
+    encoders = {
+        'base64': email.encoders.encode_base64,
+        '7or8bit': email.encoders.encode_7or8bit,
+    }
+    if encoding not in encoders:
+        raise ValueError(
+            'Unsupported multipart encoding: %s. Must be one of: %s' % (encoding, ', '.join(sorted(encoders)))
+        )
+    return encoders[encoding]
+
+
+def prepare_multipart(fields, multipart_encoding=None):
     """Takes a mapping, and prepares a multipart/form-data body
 
     :arg fields: Mapping
+    :arg multipart_encoding: str
     :returns: tuple of (content_type, body) where ``content_type`` is
         the ``multipart/form-data`` ``Content-Type`` header including
         ``boundary`` and ``body`` is the prepared bytestring body
 
-    Payload content from a file will be base64 encoded and will include
-    the appropriate ``Content-Transfer-Encoding`` and ``Content-Type``
+    Payload content from a file will be encoded using the specified
+    ``multipart_encoding`` (base64 by default) and will include the
+    appropriate ``Content-Transfer-Encoding`` and ``Content-Type``
     headers.
 
     Example:
@@ -1036,6 +1059,11 @@ def prepare_multipart(fields):
             'Mapping is required, cannot be type %s' % fields.__class__.__name__
         )
 
+    if multipart_encoding is None:
+        multipart_encoding = 'base64'
+
+    encoder = set_multipart_encoding(multipart_encoding)
+
     m = email.mime.multipart.MIMEMultipart('form-data')
     for field, value in sorted(fields.items()):
         if isinstance(value, str):
@@ -1063,9 +1091,16 @@ def prepare_multipart(fields):
 
         if not content and filename:
             with open(to_bytes(filename, errors='surrogate_or_strict'), 'rb') as f:
-                part = email.mime.application.MIMEApplication(f.read())
-                del part['Content-Type']
-                part.add_header('Content-Type', '%s/%s' % (main_type, sub_type))
+                data = f.read()
+            part = email.mime.application.MIMEApplication(data)
+            del part['Content-Type']
+            part.add_header('Content-Type', '%s/%s' % (main_type, sub_type))
+            # Reset the payload to the raw data so that the chosen encoder
+            # (base64 by default) can encode it, instead of re-encoding the
+            # base64 payload set by MIMEApplication.
+            del part['Content-Transfer-Encoding']
+            part.set_payload(data)
+            encoder(part)
         else:
             part = email.mime.nonmultipart.MIMENonMultipart(main_type, sub_type)
             part.set_payload(to_bytes(content))

+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+
+# Copyright: (c) 2024, Ansible Project
+# GNU General Public License v3.0+ (see COPYING or https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.txt)
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+DOCUMENTATION = r'''
+---
+module: mount_facts
+version_added: 2.18
+short_description: Gather detailed information about filesystem mounts
+description:
+  - Retrieves detailed information about mounted filesystems from various static and dynamic sources on a POSIX host.
+  - Provides advanced filtering by device and filesystem type using fnmatch patterns.
+  - Allows for configurable timeouts and handling of duplicate mount point entries.
+  - Unlike the default C(ansible_mounts) fact, mounts with non-standard device names (for example GPFS or FUSE mounts) are not filtered out.
+options:
+  devices:
+    description:
+      - List of fnmatch patterns used to filter the gathered mounts by device name.
+      - Only mounts whose device matches at least one of the patterns are returned.
+      - When empty (the default), all devices are returned.
+    type: list
+    elements: str
+    default: []
+  fstypes:
+    description:
+      - List of fnmatch patterns used to filter the gathered mounts by filesystem type.
+      - Only mounts whose filesystem type matches at least one of the patterns are returned.
+      - When empty (the default), all filesystem types are returned.
+    type: list
+    elements: str
+    default: []
+  sources:
+    description:
+      - List of sources to gather mount information from.
+      - Each entry can be the path of a file containing mtab style entries (for example C(/etc/fstab) or C(/proc/mounts))
+        or one of the aliases C(all), C(static) and C(dynamic).
+      - The C(static) alias expands to C(/etc/fstab) and C(/etc/mtab).
+      - The C(dynamic) alias expands to C(/proc/mounts).
+      - The C(all) alias expands to both C(static) and C(dynamic).
+    type: list
+    elements: str
+    default: ['all']
+  mount_binary:
+    description:
+      - Path to the C(mount) executable to use as an additional dynamic source.
+      - The module executes the binary without arguments and parses its output.
+      - When not set, no mount binary is executed.
+    type: str
+    default: null
+  timeout:
+    description:
+      - Maximum time in seconds to wait while gathering the mount information.
+      - When the timeout is exceeded, the action defined by V(on_timeout) is taken.
+      - When not set, no timeout is applied.
+    type: float
+    default: null
+  on_timeout:
+    description:
+      - Action to take when the gathering V(timeout) is exceeded.
+      - V(error) fails the module.
+      - V(warn) emits a warning and returns the partial results gathered so far.
+      - V(ignore) silently returns the partial results gathered so far.
+    type: str
+    choices: [error, warn, ignore]
+    default: warn
+  include_aggregate_mounts:
+    description:
+      - Whether to include the RV(ansible_facts.aggregate_mounts) list, containing all discovered mounts including duplicates, in the results.
+      - When this option is not explicitly set and duplicate mount points are discovered, a warning is emitted.
+    type: bool
+    default: null
+author:
+  - Ansible Project (@ansible)
+'''
+
+EXAMPLES = r'''
+- name: Gather mount facts
+  ansible.legacy.mount_facts:
+  register: result
+
+- name: Gather mount facts for specific devices and filesystem types
+  ansible.legacy.mount_facts:
+    devices:
+      - "/dev/*"
+      - "store*"
+    fstypes:
+      - "ext*"
+      - "gpfs"
+
+- name: Gather mount facts from specific sources
+  ansible.legacy.mount_facts:
+    sources:
+      - /etc/fstab
+      - /proc/mounts
+    include_aggregate_mounts: true
+
+- name: Gather mount facts with a timeout
+  ansible.legacy.mount_facts:
+    timeout: 5
+    on_timeout: error
+'''
+
+RETURN = r'''
+ansible_facts:
+  description: The gathered mount facts.
+  returned: always
+  type: dict
+  contains:
+    mount_points:
+      description:
+        - Dictionary of unique mount points, keyed by the mount point path.
+        - Each value is a dictionary describing the mount, including its device,
+          filesystem type, options, source, uuid and, when available, disk usage
+          statistics (size_total and size_available).
+      type: dict
+    aggregate_mounts:
+      description:
+        - List of all discovered mounts, including duplicate mount point entries.
+      type: list
+      returned: when V(include_aggregate_mounts) is true
+'''
+
+import fnmatch
+import os
+import re
+import time
+
+from ansible.module_utils.basic import AnsibleModule
+from ansible.module_utils.common.text.converters import to_text
+
+# file based sources that describe statically configured mounts
+STATIC_SOURCES = ('/etc/fstab', '/etc/mtab')
+# file based sources that describe the currently mounted filesystems
+DYNAMIC_SOURCES = ('/proc/mounts',)
+
+# regex used against mount binary output to parse entries, e.g.
+# /dev/mapper/rootvg-root on / type ext4 (rw,relatime)
+MOUNT_BINARY_RE = re.compile(r'^(\S+) on (\S+) type (\S+) \(([^)]*)\)')
+
+
+def parse_mount_line(line, source):
+    """Parse a single mtab/fstab style line into a mount entry.
+
+    Returns None when the line is not a valid mount entry.
+    """
+    line = line.strip()
+    if not line or line.startswith('#'):
+        return None
+
+    fields = line.split()
+    if len(fields) < 3:
+        return None
+
+    device, mount, fstype = fields[0], fields[1], fields[2]
+    options = fields[3] if len(fields) > 3 else 'rw'
+
+    return {
+        'device': device,
+        'mount': mount,
+        'fstype': fstype,
+        'options': options,
+        'source': source,
+    }
+
+
+def parse_mount_binary_line(line, source):
+    """Parse a single line of mount binary output into a mount entry.
+
+    Returns None when the line does not match the expected format.
+    """
+    match = MOUNT_BINARY_RE.match(line.strip())
+    if match is None:
+        return None
+
+    device, mount, fstype, options = match.groups()
+
+    return {
+        'device': device,
+        'mount': mount,
+        'fstype': fstype,
+        'options': options,
+        'source': source,
+    }
+
+
+def expand_sources(sources):
+    """Expand the source aliases into a list of concrete source paths."""
+    expanded = []
+    for source in sources:
+        if source == 'all':
+            expanded.extend(STATIC_SOURCES)
+            expanded.extend(DYNAMIC_SOURCES)
+        elif source == 'static':
+            expanded.extend(STATIC_SOURCES)
+        elif source == 'dynamic':
+            expanded.extend(DYNAMIC_SOURCES)
+        else:
+            expanded.append(source)
+    return expanded
+
+
+def matches_patterns(value, patterns):
+    """Return True when value matches at least one of the fnmatch patterns."""
+    if not patterns:
+        return True
+    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(value, pattern) for pattern in patterns)
+
+
+def resolve_uuid(device):
+    """Resolve the UUID of a block device via /dev/disk/by-uuid, if possible."""
+    if not device.startswith('/'):
+        return 'N/A'
+
+    try:
+        uuids = os.listdir('/dev/disk/by-uuid')
+    except OSError:
+        return 'N/A'
+
+    try:
+        device_path = os.path.realpath(device)
+    except (OSError, ValueError):
+        return 'N/A'
+
+    for uuid in uuids:
+        try:
+            if os.path.realpath('/dev/disk/by-uuid/' + uuid) == device_path:
+                return uuid
+        except OSError:
+            continue
+
+    return 'N/A'
+
+
+def get_mount_size(mount):
+    """Return the (size_total, size_available) of a mount point or (None, None)."""
+    try:
+        stats = os.statvfs(mount)
+    except (OSError, AttributeError):
+        return None, None
+
+    return stats.f_blocks * stats.f_frsize, stats.f_bavail * stats.f_frsize
+
+
+def enrich_mount(mount):
+    """Add uuid and disk usage information to a mount entry."""
+    mount['uuid'] = resolve_uuid(mount['device'])
+
+    size_total, size_available = get_mount_size(mount['mount'])
+    if size_total is not None:
+        mount['size_total'] = size_total
+        mount['size_available'] = size_available
+
+    return mount
+
+
+def gather_mounts(module, sources, mount_binary, deadline):
+    """Gather mount entries from the given sources.
+
+    Returns a tuple of (mounts, timed_out) where mounts is the list of
+    gathered mount entries and timed_out indicates whether the deadline
+    was exceeded while gathering.
+    """
+    mounts = []
+    timed_out = False
+
+    def deadline_reached():
+        nonlocal timed_out
+        if deadline is not None and time.monotonic() > deadline:
+            timed_out = True
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    for source in sources:
+        if deadline_reached():
+            break
+
+        if not os.path.isfile(source) or not os.access(source, os.R_OK):
+            module.warn("Mount source %s does not exist or is not readable, skipping." % source)
+            continue
+
+        try:
+            with open(source, 'r', errors='surrogate_then_replace') as source_file:
+                for line in source_file:
+                    if deadline_reached():
+                        break
+                    entry = parse_mount_line(line, source)
+                    if entry is not None:

+            fstypes=dict(type='list', elements='str', default=[]),

+            mount_binary=dict(type='str', default=None),
+            timeout=dict(type='float', default=None),
+            on_timeout=dict(type='str', choices=['error', 'warn', 'ignore'], default='warn'),

+
+    module.exit_json(ansible_facts=ansible_facts)

+    main()

+# Copyright (c) 2021, Ansible Project
+# GNU General Public License v3.0+ (see COPYING or https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.txt)
+
+from __future__ import absolute_import, division, print_function
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+from ansible.module_utils.common.text.converters import to_native
+
+
+def get_best_parsable_locale(module, preferences=None):
+    """
+    Find the best locale for parsing command output.
+
+    :arg module: Ansible module (or compatible object exposing ``get_bin_path``
+        and ``run_command``)
+    :arg preferences: optional ordered list of locale names to try, in order of
+        preference. Defaults to ``['C.utf8', 'en_US.utf8', 'C', 'POSIX']``.
+    :return: the name of the best available locale for parsing command output
+    :raises RuntimeWarning: if the ``locale`` tool is unavailable, unusable, or
+        returns no output
+    """
+    if preferences is None:
+        preferences = ['C.utf8', 'en_US.utf8', 'C', 'POSIX']
+
+    # Locate the system ``locale`` executable
+    locale_path = module.get_bin_path("locale")
+    if locale_path is None:
+        raise RuntimeWarning("Unable to find the 'locale' command")
+
+    # Enumerate the locales installed on the system
+    rc, stdout, stderr = module.run_command([locale_path, "-a"])
+    if rc != 0:
+        raise RuntimeWarning(
+            "Error running 'locale -a' (rc=%s): %s" % (rc, to_native(stderr)))
+    if not stdout:
+        raise RuntimeWarning("The 'locale -a' command returned no output")
+
+    # Parse the available locales, ignoring blank lines
+    available_locales = [line for line in stdout.splitlines() if line]
+
+    # Select the first preferred locale that is actually available
+    for preference in preferences:
+        if preference in available_locales:
+            return preference
+
+    # Fall back to 'C' even if it is not listed by ``locale -a``
+    return "C"

+#!/usr/bin/python
+# Copyright: (c) 2018, Pluribus Networks
+# GNU General Public License v3.0+ (see COPYING or https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.txt)
+
+from __future__ import absolute_import, division, print_function
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+
+ANSIBLE_METADATA = {'metadata_version': '1.1',
+                    'status': ['preview'],
+                    'supported_by': 'community'}
+
+
+DOCUMENTATION = """
+---
+module: pn_user
+author: "Pluribus Networks (@rajaspachipulusu17)"
+version_added: "2.8"
+short_description: CLI command to manage users on Pluribus Networks
+description:
+  - This module is used to manage users on Pluribus Networks.
+options:
+  pn_cliswitch:
+    description:
+      - Target switch to run the CLI on.
+    required: False
+    type: str
+  state:
+    description:
+      - State the action to perform. Use C(present) to create a user,
+        C(absent) to delete a user and C(update) to modify a user.
+    required: True
+    type: str
+    choices: ['present', 'absent', 'update']
+  pn_name:
+    description:
+      - Name of the user.
+    required: False
+    type: str
+  pn_password:
+    description:
+      - Password of the user.
+    required: False
+    type: str
+  pn_scope:
+    description:
+      - Scope of the user.
+    required: False
+    type: str
+    choices: ['local', 'fabric']
+"""
+
+EXAMPLES = """
+- name: Create a user
+  pn_user:
+    pn_cliswitch: "sw01"
+    state: "present"
+    pn_name: "foo"
+    pn_scope: "local"
+    pn_password: "test123"
+
+- name: Update a user
+  pn_user:
+    pn_cliswitch: "sw01"
+    state: "update"
+    pn_name: "foo"
+    pn_password: "test1234"
+
+- name: Delete a user
+  pn_user:
+    pn_cliswitch: "sw01"
+    state: "absent"
+    pn_name: "foo"
+"""
+
+RETURN = """
+command:
+  description: the CLI command run on the target node.
+  returned: always
+  type: str
+stdout:
+  description: set of responses from the user command.
+  returned: always
+  type: list
+stderr:
+  description: set of error responses from the user command.
+  returned: on error
+  type: list
+changed:
+  description: indicates whether the CLI caused changes on the target.
+  returned: always
+  type: bool
+"""
+
+from ansible.module_utils.basic import AnsibleModule
+from ansible.module_utils.network.netvisor.pn_nvos import pn_cli, run_cli
+
+
+def check_cli(module, cli):
+    """
+    This method checks for idempotency using the user-show command.
+    If a user with given name exists, return True else False.
+    :param module: The Ansible module to fetch input parameters
+    :param cli: The CLI string
+    """
+    name = module.params['pn_name']
+
+    cli += ' user-show name %s format name no-show-headers' % name
+    out = module.run_command(cli.split(), use_unsafe_shell=True)[1]
+
+    out = out.split()
+
+    return True if name in out else False
+
+
+def main():
+    """ This section is for arguments parsing """
+
+    global state_map
+    state_map = dict(
+        present='user-create',
+        absent='user-delete',
+        update='user-modify'
+    )
+
+    module = AnsibleModule(
+        argument_spec=dict(
+            pn_cliswitch=dict(required=False, type='str'),
+            state=dict(required=True, type='str',
+                       choices=state_map.keys()),
+            pn_name=dict(required=False, type='str'),
+            pn_password=dict(required=False, type='str', no_log=True),
+            pn_scope=dict(required=False, type='str',
+                          choices=['local', 'fabric']),
+        ),
+        required_if=(
+            ["state", "present", ["pn_name", "pn_scope"]],
+            ["state", "absent", ["pn_name"]],
+            ["state", "update", ["pn_name", "pn_password"]]
+        )
+    )
+
+    # Accessing the arguments
+    cliswitch = module.params['pn_cliswitch']
+    state = module.params['state']
+    name = module.params['pn_name']
+    password = module.params['pn_password']
+    scope = module.params['pn_scope']
+
+    command = state_map[state]
+
+    # Building the CLI command string
+    cli = pn_cli(module, cliswitch)
+
+    USER_EXISTS = check_cli(module, cli)
+    cli += ' %s name %s ' % (command, name)
+
+    if command == 'user-create':
+        if USER_EXISTS is True:
+            module.exit_json(
+                changed=False,
+                msg='user with name %s already exists' % name
+            )
+        cli += ' scope ' + scope
+        cli += ' password ' + password
+
+    if command == 'user-delete':
+        if USER_EXISTS is False:
+            module.exit_json(
+                changed=False,
+                msg='user with name %s does not exist' % name
+            )
+
+    if command == 'user-modify':
+        if USER_EXISTS is False:
+            module.fail_json(
+                failed=True,
+                msg='user with name %s does not exist' % name
+            )
+        cli += ' password ' + password
+
+    run_cli(module, cli, state_map)
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

diff --git a/lib/ansible/modules/network/icx/icx_linkagg.py b/lib/ansible/modules/network/icx/icx_linkagg.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..696011d5ab
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/ansible/modules/network/icx/icx_linkagg.py
@@ -0,0 +1,331 @@
+#!/usr/bin/python
+# Copyright: (c) 2019, Ansible Project
+# GNU General Public License v3.0+ (see COPYING or https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.txt)
+
+from __future__ import absolute_import, division, print_function
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+ANSIBLE_METADATA = {'metadata_version': '1.1',
+                    'status': ['preview'],
+                    'supported_by': 'community'}
+
+DOCUMENTATION = """
+---
+module: icx_linkagg
+short_description: Manage Link Aggregation Groups (LAG) on Ruckus ICX network appliances
+description:
+  - This module manages the Link Aggregation Groups (LAG) configurations on
+    Ruckus ICX network appliances.
+version_added: "2.9"
+author: Ansible Network Engineering (@ansible)
+options:
+  aggregate:
+    description:
+      - The ordered set of link aggregation definitions.
+    type: list
+  purge:
+    description:
+      - Instructs the module to purge any LAGs that are not defined in the
+        desired configuration.
+    type: bool
+    default: False
+  check_running_config:
+    description:
+      - Instructs the module to compare the desired configuration against the
+        device running configuration.
+    type: bool
+    default: False
+  group:
+    description:
+      - The LAG group identifier.
+    type: str
+  name:
+    description:
+      - The name of the LAG.
+    type: str
+  mode:
+    description:
+      - The LAG mode.
+    type: str
+    choices: ['dynamic', 'static']
+  state:
+    description:
+      - The desired state of the LAG.
+    type: str
+    choices: ['present', 'absent']
+    default: present
+  members:
+    description:
+      - The list of port members for the LAG.
+    type: list
+"""
+
+EXAMPLES = """
+- name: Create a LAG
+  icx_linkagg:
+    group: 1
+    name: lag1
+    mode: static
+    members:
+      - ethernet 1/1/1
+      - ethernet 1/1/2
+    state: present
+
+- name: Create multiple LAGs and purge others
+  icx_linkagg:
+    aggregate:
+      - group: 1
+        name: lag1
+        mode: static
+        members:
+          - ethernet 1/1/1
+          - ethernet 1/1/2
+      - group: 2
+        name: lag2
+        mode: dynamic
+        members:
+          - ethernet 1/1/3
+    purge: true
+
+- name: Delete a LAG
+  icx_linkagg:
+    group: 1
+    name: lag1
+    mode: static
+    state: absent
+"""
+
+RETURN = """
+commands:
+  description: The list of commands to be sent to the device.
+  returned: always
+  type: list
+  sample: ['lag lag1 static id 1', 'ports ethernet 1/1/1', 'exit']
+"""
+
+import re
+
+from ansible.module_utils.basic import AnsibleModule
+from ansible.module_utils.network.icx.icx import get_config, run_commands, load_config
+
+
+def range_to_members(ranges, prefix=''):
+    """Convert a port range string to a list of individual member ports.
+
+    Supports single port and range formats (e.g. 'ethernet 1/1/4 to
+    ethernet 1/1/7').  Handles the 'ethe' abbreviation used in device
+    configuration.  A prefix may be applied to each member if specified.
+    """
+    members = []
+    for item in ranges.split(','):
+        item = item.strip()
+        if not item:
+            continue
+        if ' to ' in item:
+            start, end = item.split(' to ')
+            start = start.strip()
+            end = end.strip()
+            start_num = int(re.search(r'(\d+)$', start).group(1))
+            end_num = int(re.search(r'(\d+)$', end).group(1))
+            start_prefix = start[:len(start) - len(str(start_num))]
+            for i in range(start_num, end_num + 1):
+                members.append(start_prefix + str(i))
+        else:
+            members.append(item)
+    if prefix:
+        members = [prefix + member for member in members]
+    return members
+
+
+def search_obj_in_list(group, lst):
+    """Search for a configuration object with a matching group ID.
+
+    Returns the matching object if found, otherwise None.
+    """
+    for obj in lst:
+        if obj.get('group') == group:
+            return obj
+    return None
+
+
+def is_member(member, lst):
+    """Determine if a member is represented in a list of port range defs.
+
+    Each entry in the list is expanded using range_to_members so that a
+    single port (e.g. 'ethernet 1/1/2') is detected inside a range
+    definition (e.g. 'ethernet 1/1/1 to ethernet 1/1/4').  Handles the
+    'ethe' abbreviation used in device configuration.
+    """
+    member_norm = re.sub(r'\bethe\b', 'ethernet', member)
+    for item in lst:
+        item_norm = re.sub(r'\bethe\b', 'ethernet', item)
+        if member_norm in range_to_members(item_norm):
+            return True
+    return False
+
+
+def map_config_to_obj(module):
+    """Map the current device configuration to an object structure.
+
+    Parses the output of get_config for lines of the form
+    'lag <name> <mode> id <group>' followed by 'ports' (and 'disable')
+    lines.  Returns a dictionary with the LAG group ID as the key and the
+    LAG object (group, name, mode, state and members) as the value.
+    """
+    obj = {}
+    if not module.params['check_running_config']:
+        return obj
+    config = get_config(module)
+    current_lag = None
+    for line in config.splitlines():
+        if not line.strip():
+            continue
+        stripped = line.strip()
+        lag_match = re.match(r'lag (\S+) (\S+) id (\S+)', stripped)
+        if lag_match:
+            name = lag_match.group(1)
+            mode = lag_match.group(2)
+            group = lag_match.group(3)
+            current_lag = {
+                'group': group,
+                'name': name,
+                'mode': mode,
+                'state': 'present',
+                'members': [],
+            }
+            obj[group] = current_lag
+            continue
+        if stripped.startswith('ports') and current_lag is not None:
+            ports_str = stripped[len('ports'):].strip()
+            ports_str = re.sub(r'\bethe\b', 'ethernet', ports_str)
+            current_lag['members'] = range_to_members(ports_str)
+            continue
+        # any other line (e.g. 'disable') is ignored
+    return obj
+
+
+def map_params_to_obj(module):
+    """Map the module parameters to a list of LAG objects.
+
+    Supports both the aggregate form (a list of LAG definitions) and the
+    non-aggregate form (single set of parameters).  The group value is
+    normalized to string format.
+    """
+    objs = []
+    if module.params['aggregate']:
+        for item in module.params['aggregate']:
+            objs.append({
+                'group': str(item['group']),
+                'name': item['name'],
+                'mode': item['mode'],
+                'state': item.get('state', 'present'),
+                'members': item.get('members') or [],
+            })
+    else:
+        objs.append({
+            'group': str(module.params['group']),
+            'name': module.params['name'],
+            'mode': module.params['mode'],
+            'state': module.params['state'],
+            'members': module.params['members'] or [],
+        })
+    return objs
+
+
+def map_obj_to_commands(updates, module):
+    """Map the desired and current state to a list of configuration commands.
+
+    updates is a tuple of (want, have) where want is a list of desired LAG
+    objects and have is a dictionary of current LAG objects keyed by group.
+    """
+    want, have = updates
+    commands = []
+    have_list = list(have.values()) if have else []
+
+    for obj in want:
+        group = obj['group']
+        name = obj['name']
+        mode = obj['mode']
+        state = obj['state']
+        members = obj.get('members') or []
+
+        existing = search_obj_in_list(group, have_list)
+
+        if state == 'absent':
+            if existing:
+                commands.append('no lag {0} {1} id {2}'.format(
+                    existing['name'], existing['mode'], group))
+        elif state == 'present':
+            if not existing:
+                # create the LAG
+                commands.append('lag {0} {1} id {2}'.format(name, mode, group))
+                if members:
+                    commands.append('ports ' + ' '.join(members))
+                commands.append('exit')
+            else:
+                # modify the LAG members
+                have_members = existing.get('members') or []
+                removed = [m for m in have_members if not is_member(m, members)]
+                added = [m for m in members if not is_member(m, have_members)]
+                if removed or added:
+                    commands.append('lag {0} {1} id {2}'.format(name, mode, group))
+                    for member in removed:
+                        commands.append('no ports ' + member)
+                    if added:
+                        commands.append('ports ' + ' '.join(added))
+                    commands.append('exit')
+
+    if module.params['purge']:
+        want_groups = set(w['group'] for w in want)
+        for group, obj in have.items():
+            if group not in want_groups:
+                commands.append('no lag {0} {1} id {2}'.format(
+                    obj['name'], obj['mode'], group))
+
+    return commands
+
+
+def main():
+    """Main entry point for module execution."""
+    argument_spec = dict(
+        aggregate=dict(type='list'),
+        purge=dict(type='bool', default=False),
+        check_running_config=dict(type='bool', default=False),
+        group=dict(type='str'),
+        name=dict(type='str'),
+        mode=dict(type='str', choices=['dynamic', 'static']),
+        state=dict(type='str', choices=['present', 'absent'], default='present'),
+        members=dict(type='list'),
+    )
+
+    module = AnsibleModule(
+        argument_spec=argument_spec,
+        supports_check_mode=True,
+    )
+
+    if not module.params['aggregate'] and not (
+            module.params['group'] and module.params['name']
+            and module.params['mode']):
+        module.fail_json(msg='group, name and mode are required when '
+                             'aggregate is not specified')
+
+    result = {'changed': False}
+
+    # ensure the connection is in a clean state before processing
+    run_commands(module, 'skip')
+
+    want = map_params_to_obj(module)
+    have = map_config_to_obj(module)
+    commands = map_obj_to_commands((want, have), module)
+    result['commands'] = commands
+
+    if commands:
+        result['changed'] = True
+        if not module.check_mode:
+            load_config(module, commands)
+
+    module.exit_json(**result)
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+def sanitize_keys(obj, no_log_strings, ignore_keys=frozenset()):
+    """
+    Companion to :meth:`remove_values`.

+    :arg obj: The object to strip keys from.  If this is a container type,

+        container type, returns a new empty container with the same type.

+        is passed in is correct.  For instance, higher level containers need
+        to be passed in before lower level containers. For example, given
+        ``{'level1': {'level2': 'level3': [True]} }`` first pass in the
+        dictionary for ``level1``, then the dict for ``level2``, and finally
+        the list for ``level3``.

+        if isinstance(new_data, Mapping):
+            for old_key, old_elem in old_data.items():
+                new_key = _sanitize_conditions(old_key, no_log_strings, ignore_keys, deferred_removals)
+                new_elem = _sanitize_conditions(old_elem, no_log_strings, ignore_keys, deferred_removals)
+                new_data[new_key] = new_elem
+        else:
+            for elem in old_data:
+                new_elem = _sanitize_conditions(elem, no_log_strings, ignore_keys, deferred_removals)
+                if isinstance(new_data, MutableSequence):
+                    new_data.append(new_elem)
+                elif isinstance(new_data, MutableSet):
+                    new_data.add(new_elem)

+        this function so that more entries can be added to it if value is

+        element is the ``value`` parameter and the second value is a new
+        container to copy the elements of ``value`` into once iterated.

+        container type, returns a new empty container with the same type.

+

+        is passed in is correct.  For instance, higher level containers need
+        to be passed in before lower level containers. For example, given
+        ``{'level1': {'level2': 'level3': [True]} }`` first pass in the
+        dictionary for ``level1``, then the dict for ``level2``, and finally
+        the list for ``level3``.

+        elif isinstance(value, binary_type):

+def _replace_stderr_clixml(stderr: bytes) -> bytes:
+    """
+    Replace any CLIXML encoded blocks in the given stderr with their decoded
+    content.
+
+    When a command is run on a Windows host the stderr may contain CLIXML
+    encoded blocks, either on their own or mixed with other output. This
+    function scans the stderr line by line, identifies any complete CLIXML
+    blocks, decodes them with :func:`_parse_clixml` and replaces the block
+    with the decoded text. Any data that is not part of a valid, complete
+    CLIXML block (such as surrounding text or incomplete blocks) is left
+    unchanged.
+
+    :arg bytes stderr: The raw stderr bytes to process.
+    :rtype: bytes
+    :return: The stderr with any complete CLIXML blocks replaced by their
+        decoded content. If no CLIXML blocks are present the input is
+        returned unchanged.
+    """
+    lines = stderr.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    result: list[bytes] = []
+    idx = 0
+    while idx < len(lines):
+        line = lines[idx]
+        # A CLIXML block starts with a line that only contains the header.
+        if line.rstrip(b"\r\n") != b"#< CLIXML":
+            result.append(line)
+            idx += 1
+            continue
+
+        # Collect the lines that make up the CLIXML block. The block ends
+        # with the first line that contains the closing '</Objs>' tag.
+        block = [line]
+        end_idx = idx + 1
+        while end_idx < len(lines) and b"</Objs>" not in lines[end_idx]:
+            block.append(lines[end_idx])
+            end_idx += 1
+
+        if end_idx >= len(lines):
+            # The CLIXML block is incomplete (no closing tag), leave the
+            # data unchanged.
+            result.append(line)
+            idx += 1
+            continue
+
+        last_line = lines[end_idx]
+        tag_end = last_line.find(b"</Objs>") + len(b"</Objs>")
+        trailing = last_line[tag_end:]
+        block.append(last_line[:tag_end])
+
+        try:
+            try:
+                clixml_text = b"".join(block).decode("utf-8")
+            except UnicodeDecodeError:
+                clixml_text = b"".join(block).decode("cp437")
+            decoded = _parse_clixml(clixml_text.encode("utf-8"))
+        except Exception:
+            # The CLIXML block could not be parsed, leave it unchanged.
+            result.extend(block)
+            result.append(trailing)
+            idx = end_idx + 1
+            continue
+
+        result.append(decoded)
+        result.append(trailing)
+        idx = end_idx + 1
+
+    return b"".join(result)
+

+import { logger } from 'matrix-js-sdk/src/logger';
+import SettingsStore from '../../settings/SettingsStore';
+
+/**
+ * Events emitted by an HTMLMediaElement that indicate a problem with the call
+ * sound (eg. the audio failed to load or decode). These are always reported
+ * as errors.
+ */
+const ERROR_EVENTS = new Set<string>([
+    "error",
+]);
+
+/**
+ * Events emitted by an HTMLMediaElement that are not errors in themselves but
+ * are useful to see when debugging call sounds. These are only reported when
+ * the `debug_legacy_call_handler` setting is enabled.
+ */
+const DEBUG_EVENTS = new Set<string>([
+    "abort",
+    "canplay",
+    "canplaythrough",
+    "durationchange",
+    "emptied",
+    "ended",
+    "loadeddata",
+    "loadedmetadata",
+    "loadstart",
+    "pause",
+    "play",
+    "playing",
+    "progress",
+    "ratechange",
+    "seeked",
+    "seeking",
+    "stalled",
+    "suspend",
+    "timeupdate",
+    "volumechange",
+    "waiting",
+]);
+
+/**
+ * Public listener for HTMLMediaElement events, used to keep an eye on the
+ * audio elements that play the call sounds (ring, ringback, busy, call-end).
+ *
+ * It dispatches by `e.type`:
+ * - error-class events (eg. `error`) are logged as structured errors,
+ *   including the id of the element the event originated from;
+ * - debug-class events (eg. `pause`, `play`, `ended`) are logged as debug
+ *   messages, but only when the `debug_legacy_call_handler` setting is enabled;
+ * - any other events are ignored.
+ *
+ * It is safe to attach this function directly to a media element, eg.
+ * `audioElement.addEventListener("error", handleEvent)`.
+ *
+ * @param e The event emitted by an HTMLMediaElement.
+ */
+export function handleEvent(e: Event): void {
+    const target = e.target as HTMLMediaElement | null;
+    const elementId = target?.id || "unknown";
+
+    if (ERROR_EVENTS.has(e.type)) {
+        logger.error(`LegacyCallHandler: ${e.type} event on call sound audio element "${elementId}"`, e);
+    } else if (DEBUG_EVENTS.has(e.type)) {
+        if (SettingsStore.getValue("debug_legacy_call_handler")) {
+            logger.debug(`LegacyCallHandler: ${e.type} event on call sound audio element "${elementId}"`);
+        }

+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+	"time"

+	"github.com/opencontainers/go-digest"
+	ocispec "github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/specs-go/v1"
+	"oras.land/oras-go/v2/content"
+	ocilayout "oras.land/oras-go/v2/content/oci"
+	"oras.land/oras-go/v2/registry"

+
+// Option is a generic option for configuring a Store operation.
+type Option[T any] func(*T)
+
+// FetchOptions contains the options for a Store.Fetch operation.
+type FetchOptions struct {
+	// IfNoneMatch is the digest to compare against the (normalized) manifest
+	// digest. When it matches, the fetch is a no-op and no content is
+	// transferred from the underlying store.
+	IfNoneMatch digest.Digest
+}
+
+// IfNoMatch returns an Option which causes Fetch to return early (without
+// transferring any bundle content) when the manifest digest matches the
+// provided digest. This is used to implement digest-aware caching.
+func IfNoMatch(d digest.Digest) Option[FetchOptions] {
+	return func(o *FetchOptions) {
+		o.IfNoneMatch = d
+	}
+}
+
+// FetchResponse is the response from a Store.Fetch operation.
+type FetchResponse struct {
+	// Digest is the (normalized) digest of the manifest.
+	Digest digest.Digest
+	// Files are the files contained in the fetched bundle.
+	Files []fs.File
+	// Matched is true when the fetch was a no-op due to a digest match.
+	Matched bool
+}
+
+// storage is the interface implemented by both the remote and local OCI
+// content stores which the Store uses to resolve and fetch bundle content.
+type storage interface {
+	content.Resolver
+	content.ReadOnlyStorage
+}
+
+// Store is a generic store for fetching OCI feature bundles from either a
+// remote OCI registry (http/https) or a local OCI bundle directory (flipt).
+type Store struct {
+	// ref is the reference (tag or digest) of the bundle to fetch.
+	ref string
+	// store is the underlying OCI content store.
+	store storage
+}
+
+// NewStore returns a new Store for the given configuration.
+// The scheme of the configured repository determines the type of store which
+// is returned:
+//
+//   - http/https: a store backed by a remote OCI registry
+//   - flipt:      a store backed by a local OCI bundle directory
+//
+// Any other scheme results in an error.
+func NewStore(cfg *config.OCI) (*Store, error) {
+	u, err := url.Parse(cfg.Repository)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing repository: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	switch u.Scheme {
+	case "http", "https":
+		return newRemoteStore(cfg, u)
+	case "flipt":
+		return newLocalStore(cfg, u)
+	default:
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported scheme: %s", u.Scheme)
+	}
+}
+
+// newRemoteStore returns a Store backed by a remote OCI registry.
+func newRemoteStore(cfg *config.OCI, u *url.URL) (*Store, error) {
+	// derive a distribution reference by stripping the scheme
+	ref, err := registry.ParseReference(u.Host + u.Path)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing reference: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	repo, err := remote.NewRepository(ref.Registry + "/" + ref.Repository)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("creating repository: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	// use plain HTTP when the scheme is http or insecure is configured
+	repo.PlainHTTP = u.Scheme == "http" || cfg.Insecure
+
+	if cfg.Authentication != nil {
+		repo.Client = &auth.Client{
+			Credential: auth.StaticCredential(ref.Registry, auth.Credential{
+				Username: cfg.Authentication.Username,
+				Password: cfg.Authentication.Password,
+			}),
+		}
+	}
+
+	// default to the "latest" tag when no reference is supplied
+	resolveRef := ref.Reference
+	if resolveRef == "" {
+		resolveRef = "latest"
+	}
+
+	return &Store{
+		ref:   resolveRef,
+		store: repo,
+	}, nil
+}
+
+// newLocalStore returns a Store backed by a local OCI bundle directory.
+// The bundle is expected to live under the Flipt configuration directory in
+// a "bundles" subdirectory named after the repository host.
+func newLocalStore(cfg *config.OCI, u *url.URL) (*Store, error) {
+	dir, err := config.Dir()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("getting config dir: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	path := filepath.Join(dir, "bundles", u.Host)
+
+	store, err := ocilayout.New(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("creating local store: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	return &Store{
+		ref:   "latest",
+		store: store,
+	}, nil
+}
+
+// Fetch fetches the bundle from the store and returns the manifest digest
+// along with the bundle files. When the IfNoMatch option is supplied and the
+// manifest digest matches, the fetch is a no-op and Matched is set to true.
+func (s *Store) Fetch(ctx context.Context, opts ...Option[FetchOptions]) (*FetchResponse, error) {
+	var options FetchOptions
+	for _, opt := range opts {
+		opt(&options)
+	}
+
+	// resolve the manifest descriptor
+	manifestDesc, err := s.store.Resolve(ctx, s.ref)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolving manifest: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	// fetch the manifest content
+	manifestBytes, err := content.FetchAll(ctx, s.store, manifestDesc)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetching manifest: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	// compute the normalized manifest digest (annotations removed)
+	manifestDigest, err := digestManifest(manifestBytes)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("digesting manifest: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	// short-circuit when the digest matches (cache hit)
+	if options.IfNoneMatch != "" && options.IfNoneMatch == manifestDigest {
+		return &FetchResponse{
+			Digest:  manifestDigest,
+			Matched: true,
+		}, nil
+	}
+
+	// unmarshal the manifest to enumerate the layers
+	var manifest ocispec.Manifest
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(manifestBytes, &manifest); err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unmarshaling manifest: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	// fetch and convert each layer into a file
+	files := make([]fs.File, 0, len(manifest.Layers))
+	for _, layer := range manifest.Layers {
+		if err := validateMediaType(layer.MediaType); err != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("layer %s: %w", layer.Digest, err)
+		}
+
+		rc, err := s.store.Fetch(ctx, layer)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("fetching layer %s: %w", layer.Digest, err)
+		}
+
+		file, err := newFile(layer, rc)
+		rc.Close()
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("creating file for layer %s: %w", layer.Digest, err)
+		}
+
+		files = append(files, file)
+	}
+
+	return &FetchResponse{
+		Digest: manifestDigest,
+		Files:  files,
+	}, nil
+}
+
+// digestManifest computes the digest of a manifest after normalizing it by
+// removing its annotations. This ensures a consistent and repeatable value
+// regardless of the annotations present on the manifest.
+func digestManifest(data []byte) (digest.Digest, error) {
+	var manifest ocispec.Manifest
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &manifest); err != nil {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("unmarshaling manifest: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	// normalize by removing annotations before computing the digest
+	manifest.Annotations = nil
+
+	normalized, err := json.Marshal(&manifest)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("marshaling manifest: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	return digest.FromBytes(normalized), nil
+}
+
+// validateMediaType returns an error when the media type is missing or not a
+// recognized Flipt media type.
+func validateMediaType(mediaType string) error {
+	if mediaType == "" {
+		return ErrMissingMediaType
+	}
+
+	switch mediaType {
+	case MediaTypeFliptFeatures, MediaTypeFliptNamespace:
+		return nil
+	default:
+		return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrUnexpectedMediaType, mediaType)
+	}
+}
+
+// fileEncoding returns the encoding suffix of a media type (the part after
+// the "+"), e.g. "yaml" for "application/vnd.flipt.features.v1+yaml".
+func fileEncoding(mediaType string) string {
+	if _, enc, ok := strings.Cut(mediaType, "+"); ok {
+		return enc
+	}
+	return ""
+}
+
+// File implements fs.File for a single file (layer) in an OCI bundle.
+type File struct {
+	io.ReadCloser
+	// reader is the underlying seekable reader backing the file content.
+	reader *bytes.Reader
+	// info is the file metadata.
+	info FileInfo
+}
+
+// Seek implements the fs.File Seek method for the File type, allowing
+// repositioning within the file.
+func (f *File) Seek(offset int64, whence int) (int64, error) {
+	return f.reader.Seek(offset, whence)
+}
+
+// Stat implements the fs.File Stat method for the File type, returning its
+// metadata.
+func (f *File) Stat() (fs.FileInfo, error) {
+	return f.info, nil
+}
+
+// newFile creates a File from a layer descriptor and its content reader.
+// The content is read fully so that the resulting file is seekable.
+func newFile(desc ocispec.Descriptor, rc io.ReadCloser) (*File, error) {
+	data, err := io.ReadAll(rc)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("reading content: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	reader := bytes.NewReader(data)
+
+	return &File{
+		ReadCloser: io.NopCloser(reader),
+		reader:     reader,
+		info: FileInfo{
+			digest:   desc.Digest,
+			encoding: fileEncoding(desc.MediaType),
+			size:     desc.Size,
+			modTime:  time.Time{},
+			perm:     fs.FileMode(0o444),
+		},
+	}, nil
+}
+
+// FileInfo implements fs.FileInfo for a single file in an OCI bundle.
+type FileInfo struct {
+	digest   digest.Digest
+	encoding string
+	size     int64
+	modTime  time.Time
+	perm     fs.FileMode
+}
+
+// Name returns the name of the file, derived by concatenating the digest hex
+// value and the encoding extension (e.g. ".json", ".yaml").
+func (f FileInfo) Name() string {
+	return f.digest.Hex() + "." + f.encoding
+}
+
+// Size returns the size in bytes of the file.
+func (f FileInfo) Size() int64 {
+	return f.size
+}
+
+// Mode returns the file mode/permissions for the file.
+func (f FileInfo) Mode() fs.FileMode {
+	return f.perm
+}
+
+// ModTime returns the last modification time of the file.
+func (f FileInfo) ModTime() time.Time {
+	return f.modTime
+}
+
+// IsDir returns false as a FileInfo always represents a regular file.
+func (f FileInfo) IsDir() bool {
+	return false
+}
+
+// Sys returns the underlying data source for the file (nil).
+func (f FileInfo) Sys() any {
+	return nil
+}

diff --git a/vendor/github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/2q.go b/vendor/github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/2q.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..e474cd07
--- /dev/null
+++ b/vendor/github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/2q.go
@@ -0,0 +1,223 @@
+package lru
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"sync"
+
+	"github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/simplelru"
+)
+
+const (
+	// Default2QRecentRatio is the ratio of the 2Q cache dedicated
+	// to recently added entries that have only been accessed once.
+	Default2QRecentRatio = 0.25
+
+	// Default2QGhostEntries is the default ratio of ghost
+	// entries kept to track entries recently evicted
+	Default2QGhostEntries = 0.50
+)
+
+// TwoQueueCache is a thread-safe fixed size 2Q cache.
+// 2Q is an enhancement over the standard LRU cache
+// in that it tracks both frequently and recently used
+// entries separately. This avoids a burst in access to new
+// entries from evicting frequently used entries. It adds some
+// additional tracking overhead to the standard LRU cache, and is
+// computationally about 2x the cost, and adds some metadata over
+// head. The ARCCache is similar, but does not require setting any
+// parameters.
+type TwoQueueCache struct {
+	size       int
+	recentSize int
+
+	recent      simplelru.LRUCache
+	frequent    simplelru.LRUCache
+	recentEvict simplelru.LRUCache
+	lock        sync.RWMutex
+}
+
+// New2Q creates a new TwoQueueCache using the default
+// values for the parameters.
+func New2Q(size int) (*TwoQueueCache, error) {
+	return New2QParams(size, Default2QRecentRatio, Default2QGhostEntries)
+}
+
+// New2QParams creates a new TwoQueueCache using the provided
+// parameter values.
+func New2QParams(size int, recentRatio float64, ghostRatio float64) (*TwoQueueCache, error) {
+	if size <= 0 {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid size")
+	}
+	if recentRatio < 0.0 || recentRatio > 1.0 {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid recent ratio")
+	}
+	if ghostRatio < 0.0 || ghostRatio > 1.0 {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("invalid ghost ratio")
+	}
+
+	// Determine the sub-sizes
+	recentSize := int(float64(size) * recentRatio)
+	evictSize := int(float64(size) * ghostRatio)
+
+	// Allocate the LRUs
+	recent, err := simplelru.NewLRU(size, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	frequent, err := simplelru.NewLRU(size, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	recentEvict, err := simplelru.NewLRU(evictSize, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	// Initialize the cache
+	c := &TwoQueueCache{
+		size:        size,
+		recentSize:  recentSize,
+		recent:      recent,
+		frequent:    frequent,
+		recentEvict: recentEvict,
+	}
+	return c, nil
+}
+
+// Get looks up a key's value from the cache.
+func (c *TwoQueueCache) Get(key interface{}) (value interface{}, ok bool) {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	defer c.lock.Unlock()
+
+	// Check if this is a frequent value
+	if val, ok := c.frequent.Get(key); ok {
+		return val, ok
+	}
+
+	// If the value is contained in recent, then we
+	// promote it to frequent
+	if val, ok := c.recent.Peek(key); ok {
+		c.recent.Remove(key)
+		c.frequent.Add(key, val)
+		return val, ok
+	}
+
+	// No hit
+	return nil, false
+}
+
+// Add adds a value to the cache.
+func (c *TwoQueueCache) Add(key, value interface{}) {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	defer c.lock.Unlock()
+
+	// Check if the value is frequently used already,
+	// and just update the value
+	if c.frequent.Contains(key) {
+		c.frequent.Add(key, value)
+		return
+	}
+
+	// Check if the value is recently used, and promote
+	// the value into the frequent list
+	if c.recent.Contains(key) {
+		c.recent.Remove(key)
+		c.frequent.Add(key, value)
+		return
+	}
+
+	// If the value was recently evicted, add it to the
+	// frequently used list
+	if c.recentEvict.Contains(key) {
+		c.ensureSpace(true)
+		c.recentEvict.Remove(key)
+		c.frequent.Add(key, value)
+		return
+	}
+
+	// Add to the recently seen list
+	c.ensureSpace(false)
+	c.recent.Add(key, value)
+	return
+}
+
+// ensureSpace is used to ensure we have space in the cache
+func (c *TwoQueueCache) ensureSpace(recentEvict bool) {
+	// If we have space, nothing to do
+	recentLen := c.recent.Len()
+	freqLen := c.frequent.Len()
+	if recentLen+freqLen < c.size {
+		return
+	}
+
+	// If the recent buffer is larger than
+	// the target, evict from there
+	if recentLen > 0 && (recentLen > c.recentSize || (recentLen == c.recentSize && !recentEvict)) {
+		k, _, _ := c.recent.RemoveOldest()
+		c.recentEvict.Add(k, nil)
+		return
+	}
+
+	// Remove from the frequent list otherwise
+	c.frequent.RemoveOldest()
+}
+
+// Len returns the number of items in the cache.
+func (c *TwoQueueCache) Len() int {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	defer c.lock.RUnlock()
+	return c.recent.Len() + c.frequent.Len()
+}
+
+// Keys returns a slice of the keys in the cache.
+// The frequently used keys are first in the returned slice.
+func (c *TwoQueueCache) Keys() []interface{} {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	defer c.lock.RUnlock()
+	k1 := c.frequent.Keys()
+	k2 := c.recent.Keys()
+	return append(k1, k2...)
+}
+
+// Remove removes the provided key from the cache.
+func (c *TwoQueueCache) Remove(key interface{}) {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	defer c.lock.Unlock()
+	if c.frequent.Remove(key) {
+		return
+	}
+	if c.recent.Remove(key) {
+		return
+	}
+	if c.recentEvict.Remove(key) {
+		return
+	}
+}
+
+// Purge is used to completely clear the cache.
+func (c *TwoQueueCache) Purge() {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	defer c.lock.Unlock()
+	c.recent.Purge()
+	c.frequent.Purge()
+	c.recentEvict.Purge()
+}
+
+// Contains is used to check if the cache contains a key
+// without updating recency or frequency.
+func (c *TwoQueueCache) Contains(key interface{}) bool {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	defer c.lock.RUnlock()
+	return c.frequent.Contains(key) || c.recent.Contains(key)
+}
+
+// Peek is used to inspect the cache value of a key
+// without updating recency or frequency.
+func (c *TwoQueueCache) Peek(key interface{}) (value interface{}, ok bool) {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	defer c.lock.RUnlock()
+	if val, ok := c.frequent.Peek(key); ok {
+		return val, ok
+	}
+	return c.recent.Peek(key)
+}

+golang-lru
+==========
+
+This provides the `lru` package which implements a fixed-size
+thread safe LRU cache. It is based on the cache in Groupcache.
+
+Documentation
+=============
+
+Full docs are available on [Godoc](http://godoc.org/github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru)
+
+Example
+=======
+

+
+```go
+l, _ := New(128)
+for i := 0; i < 256; i++ {

+package lru
+
+import (
+	"sync"
+
+	"github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/simplelru"
+)
+
+// ARCCache is a thread-safe fixed size Adaptive Replacement Cache (ARC).
+// ARC is an enhancement over the standard LRU cache in that tracks both
+// frequency and recency of use. This avoids a burst in access to new
+// entries from evicting the frequently used older entries. It adds some
+// additional tracking overhead to a standard LRU cache, computationally
+// it is roughly 2x the cost, and the extra memory overhead is linear
+// with the size of the cache. ARC has been patented by IBM, but is
+// similar to the TwoQueueCache (2Q) which requires setting parameters.
+type ARCCache struct {
+	size int // Size is the total capacity of the cache
+	p    int // P is the dynamic preference towards T1 or T2
+
+	t1 simplelru.LRUCache // T1 is the LRU for recently accessed items
+	b1 simplelru.LRUCache // B1 is the LRU for evictions from t1
+
+	t2 simplelru.LRUCache // T2 is the LRU for frequently accessed items
+	b2 simplelru.LRUCache // B2 is the LRU for evictions from t2
+
+	lock sync.RWMutex
+}
+
+// NewARC creates an ARC of the given size
+func NewARC(size int) (*ARCCache, error) {
+	// Create the sub LRUs
+	b1, err := simplelru.NewLRU(size, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	b2, err := simplelru.NewLRU(size, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	t1, err := simplelru.NewLRU(size, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	t2, err := simplelru.NewLRU(size, nil)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+
+	// Initialize the ARC
+	c := &ARCCache{
+		size: size,
+		p:    0,
+		t1:   t1,
+		b1:   b1,
+		t2:   t2,
+		b2:   b2,
+	}
+	return c, nil
+}
+
+// Get looks up a key's value from the cache.
+func (c *ARCCache) Get(key interface{}) (value interface{}, ok bool) {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	defer c.lock.Unlock()
+
+	// If the value is contained in T1 (recent), then
+	// promote it to T2 (frequent)
+	if val, ok := c.t1.Peek(key); ok {
+		c.t1.Remove(key)
+		c.t2.Add(key, val)
+		return val, ok
+	}
+
+	// Check if the value is contained in T2 (frequent)
+	if val, ok := c.t2.Get(key); ok {
+		return val, ok
+	}
+
+	// No hit
+	return nil, false
+}
+
+// Add adds a value to the cache.
+func (c *ARCCache) Add(key, value interface{}) {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	defer c.lock.Unlock()
+
+	// Check if the value is contained in T1 (recent), and potentially
+	// promote it to frequent T2
+	if c.t1.Contains(key) {
+		c.t1.Remove(key)
+		c.t2.Add(key, value)
+		return
+	}
+
+	// Check if the value is already in T2 (frequent) and update it
+	if c.t2.Contains(key) {
+		c.t2.Add(key, value)
+		return
+	}
+
+	// Check if this value was recently evicted as part of the
+	// recently used list
+	if c.b1.Contains(key) {
+		// T1 set is too small, increase P appropriately
+		delta := 1
+		b1Len := c.b1.Len()
+		b2Len := c.b2.Len()
+		if b2Len > b1Len {
+			delta = b2Len / b1Len
+		}
+		if c.p+delta >= c.size {
+			c.p = c.size
+		} else {
+			c.p += delta
+		}
+
+		// Potentially need to make room in the cache
+		if c.t1.Len()+c.t2.Len() >= c.size {
+			c.replace(false)
+		}
+
+		// Remove from B1
+		c.b1.Remove(key)
+
+		// Add the key to the frequently used list
+		c.t2.Add(key, value)
+		return
+	}
+
+	// Check if this value was recently evicted as part of the
+	// frequently used list
+	if c.b2.Contains(key) {
+		// T2 set is too small, decrease P appropriately
+		delta := 1
+		b1Len := c.b1.Len()
+		b2Len := c.b2.Len()
+		if b1Len > b2Len {
+			delta = b1Len / b2Len
+		}
+		if delta >= c.p {
+			c.p = 0
+		} else {
+			c.p -= delta
+		}
+
+		// Potentially need to make room in the cache
+		if c.t1.Len()+c.t2.Len() >= c.size {
+			c.replace(true)
+		}
+
+		// Remove from B2
+		c.b2.Remove(key)
+
+		// Add the key to the frequently used list
+		c.t2.Add(key, value)
+		return
+	}
+
+	// Potentially need to make room in the cache
+	if c.t1.Len()+c.t2.Len() >= c.size {
+		c.replace(false)
+	}
+
+	// Keep the size of the ghost buffers trim
+	if c.b1.Len() > c.size-c.p {
+		c.b1.RemoveOldest()
+	}
+	if c.b2.Len() > c.p {
+		c.b2.RemoveOldest()
+	}
+
+	// Add to the recently seen list
+	c.t1.Add(key, value)
+	return
+}
+
+// replace is used to adaptively evict from either T1 or T2
+// based on the current learned value of P
+func (c *ARCCache) replace(b2ContainsKey bool) {
+	t1Len := c.t1.Len()
+	if t1Len > 0 && (t1Len > c.p || (t1Len == c.p && b2ContainsKey)) {
+		k, _, ok := c.t1.RemoveOldest()
+		if ok {
+			c.b1.Add(k, nil)
+		}
+	} else {
+		k, _, ok := c.t2.RemoveOldest()
+		if ok {
+			c.b2.Add(k, nil)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+// Len returns the number of cached entries
+func (c *ARCCache) Len() int {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	defer c.lock.RUnlock()
+	return c.t1.Len() + c.t2.Len()
+}
+
+// Keys returns all the cached keys
+func (c *ARCCache) Keys() []interface{} {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	defer c.lock.RUnlock()
+	k1 := c.t1.Keys()
+	k2 := c.t2.Keys()
+	return append(k1, k2...)
+}
+
+// Remove is used to purge a key from the cache
+func (c *ARCCache) Remove(key interface{}) {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	defer c.lock.Unlock()
+	if c.t1.Remove(key) {
+		return
+	}
+	if c.t2.Remove(key) {
+		return
+	}
+	if c.b1.Remove(key) {
+		return
+	}
+	if c.b2.Remove(key) {
+		return
+	}
+}
+
+// Purge is used to clear the cache
+func (c *ARCCache) Purge() {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	defer c.lock.Unlock()
+	c.t1.Purge()
+	c.t2.Purge()
+	c.b1.Purge()
+	c.b2.Purge()
+}
+
+// Contains is used to check if the cache contains a key
+// without updating recency or frequency.
+func (c *ARCCache) Contains(key interface{}) bool {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	defer c.lock.RUnlock()
+	return c.t1.Contains(key) || c.t2.Contains(key)
+}
+
+// Peek is used to inspect the cache value of a key
+// without updating recency or frequency.
+func (c *ARCCache) Peek(key interface{}) (value interface{}, ok bool) {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	defer c.lock.RUnlock()
+	if val, ok := c.t1.Peek(key); ok {
+		return val, ok
+	}
+	return c.t2.Peek(key)
+}

+// Package lru provides three different LRU caches of varying sophistication.
+//
+// Cache is a simple LRU cache. It is based on the
+// LRU implementation in groupcache:
+// https://github.com/golang/groupcache/tree/master/lru
+//
+// TwoQueueCache tracks frequently used and recently used entries separately.
+// This avoids a burst of accesses from taking out frequently used entries,
+// at the cost of about 2x computational overhead and some extra bookkeeping.
+//
+// ARCCache is an adaptive replacement cache. It tracks recent evictions as
+// well as recent usage in both the frequent and recent caches. Its
+// computational overhead is comparable to TwoQueueCache, but the memory
+// overhead is linear with the size of the cache.
+//
+// ARC has been patented by IBM, so do not use it if that is problematic for
+// your program.
+//
+// All caches in this package take locks while operating, and are therefore
+// thread-safe for consumers.
+package lru

+package lru
+
+import (
+	"sync"
+
+	"github.com/hashicorp/golang-lru/simplelru"
+)
+
+// Cache is a thread-safe fixed size LRU cache.
+type Cache struct {
+	lru  simplelru.LRUCache
+	lock sync.RWMutex
+}
+
+// New creates an LRU of the given size.
+func New(size int) (*Cache, error) {
+	return NewWithEvict(size, nil)
+}
+
+// NewWithEvict constructs a fixed size cache with the given eviction
+// callback.
+func NewWithEvict(size int, onEvicted func(key interface{}, value interface{})) (*Cache, error) {
+	lru, err := simplelru.NewLRU(size, simplelru.EvictCallback(onEvicted))
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	c := &Cache{
+		lru: lru,
+	}
+	return c, nil
+}
+
+// Purge is used to completely clear the cache.
+func (c *Cache) Purge() {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	c.lru.Purge()
+	c.lock.Unlock()
+}
+
+// Add adds a value to the cache.  Returns true if an eviction occurred.
+func (c *Cache) Add(key, value interface{}) (evicted bool) {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	evicted = c.lru.Add(key, value)
+	c.lock.Unlock()
+	return evicted
+}
+
+// Get looks up a key's value from the cache.
+func (c *Cache) Get(key interface{}) (value interface{}, ok bool) {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	value, ok = c.lru.Get(key)
+	c.lock.Unlock()
+	return value, ok
+}
+
+// Contains checks if a key is in the cache, without updating the
+// recent-ness or deleting it for being stale.
+func (c *Cache) Contains(key interface{}) bool {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	containKey := c.lru.Contains(key)
+	c.lock.RUnlock()
+	return containKey
+}
+
+// Peek returns the key value (or undefined if not found) without updating
+// the "recently used"-ness of the key.
+func (c *Cache) Peek(key interface{}) (value interface{}, ok bool) {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	value, ok = c.lru.Peek(key)
+	c.lock.RUnlock()
+	return value, ok
+}
+
+// ContainsOrAdd checks if a key is in the cache  without updating the
+// recent-ness or deleting it for being stale,  and if not, adds the value.
+// Returns whether found and whether an eviction occurred.
+func (c *Cache) ContainsOrAdd(key, value interface{}) (ok, evicted bool) {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	defer c.lock.Unlock()
+
+	if c.lru.Contains(key) {
+		return true, false
+	}
+	evicted = c.lru.Add(key, value)
+	return false, evicted
+}
+
+// Remove removes the provided key from the cache.
+func (c *Cache) Remove(key interface{}) {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	c.lru.Remove(key)
+	c.lock.Unlock()
+}
+
+// RemoveOldest removes the oldest item from the cache.
+func (c *Cache) RemoveOldest() {
+	c.lock.Lock()
+	c.lru.RemoveOldest()
+	c.lock.Unlock()
+}
+
+// Keys returns a slice of the keys in the cache, from oldest to newest.
+func (c *Cache) Keys() []interface{} {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	keys := c.lru.Keys()
+	c.lock.RUnlock()
+	return keys
+}
+
+// Len returns the number of items in the cache.
+func (c *Cache) Len() int {
+	c.lock.RLock()
+	length := c.lru.Len()
+	c.lock.RUnlock()
+	return length
+}

+package simplelru
+
+import (
+	"container/list"
+	"errors"
+)
+
+// EvictCallback is used to get a callback when a cache entry is evicted
+type EvictCallback func(key interface{}, value interface{})
+
+// LRU implements a non-thread safe fixed size LRU cache
+type LRU struct {
+	size      int
+	evictList *list.List
+	items     map[interface{}]*list.Element
+	onEvict   EvictCallback
+}
+
+// entry is used to hold a value in the evictList
+type entry struct {
+	key   interface{}
+	value interface{}
+}
+
+// NewLRU constructs an LRU of the given size
+func NewLRU(size int, onEvict EvictCallback) (*LRU, error) {
+	if size <= 0 {
+		return nil, errors.New("Must provide a positive size")
+	}
+	c := &LRU{
+		size:      size,
+		evictList: list.New(),
+		items:     make(map[interface{}]*list.Element),
+		onEvict:   onEvict,
+	}
+	return c, nil
+}
+
+// Purge is used to completely clear the cache.
+func (c *LRU) Purge() {
+	for k, v := range c.items {
+		if c.onEvict != nil {
+			c.onEvict(k, v.Value.(*entry).value)
+		}
+		delete(c.items, k)
+	}
+	c.evictList.Init()
+}
+
+// Add adds a value to the cache.  Returns true if an eviction occurred.
+func (c *LRU) Add(key, value interface{}) (evicted bool) {
+	// Check for existing item
+	if ent, ok := c.items[key]; ok {
+		c.evictList.MoveToFront(ent)
+		ent.Value.(*entry).value = value
+		return false
+	}
+
+	// Add new item
+	ent := &entry{key, value}
+	entry := c.evictList.PushFront(ent)
+	c.items[key] = entry
+
+	evict := c.evictList.Len() > c.size
+	// Verify size not exceeded
+	if evict {
+		c.removeOldest()
+	}
+	return evict
+}
+
+// Get looks up a key's value from the cache.
+func (c *LRU) Get(key interface{}) (value interface{}, ok bool) {
+	if ent, ok := c.items[key]; ok {
+		c.evictList.MoveToFront(ent)
+		return ent.Value.(*entry).value, true
+	}
+	return
+}
+
+// Contains checks if a key is in the cache, without updating the recent-ness
+// or deleting it for being stale.
+func (c *LRU) Contains(key interface{}) (ok bool) {
+	_, ok = c.items[key]
+	return ok
+}
+
+// Peek returns the key value (or undefined if not found) without updating
+// the "recently used"-ness of the key.
+func (c *LRU) Peek(key interface{}) (value interface{}, ok bool) {
+	var ent *list.Element
+	if ent, ok = c.items[key]; ok {
+		return ent.Value.(*entry).value, true
+	}
+	return nil, ok
+}
+
+// Remove removes the provided key from the cache, returning if the
+// key was contained.
+func (c *LRU) Remove(key interface{}) (present bool) {
+	if ent, ok := c.items[key]; ok {
+		c.removeElement(ent)
+		return true
+	}
+	return false
+}
+
+// RemoveOldest removes the oldest item from the cache.
+func (c *LRU) RemoveOldest() (key interface{}, value interface{}, ok bool) {
+	ent := c.evictList.Back()
+	if ent != nil {
+		c.removeElement(ent)
+		kv := ent.Value.(*entry)
+		return kv.key, kv.value, true
+	}
+	return nil, nil, false
+}
+
+// GetOldest returns the oldest entry
+func (c *LRU) GetOldest() (key interface{}, value interface{}, ok bool) {
+	ent := c.evictList.Back()
+	if ent != nil {
+		kv := ent.Value.(*entry)
+		return kv.key, kv.value, true
+	}
+	return nil, nil, false
+}
+
+// Keys returns a slice of the keys in the cache, from oldest to newest.
+func (c *LRU) Keys() []interface{} {
+	keys := make([]interface{}, len(c.items))
+	i := 0
+	for ent := c.evictList.Back(); ent != nil; ent = ent.Prev() {
+		keys[i] = ent.Value.(*entry).key
+		i++
+	}
+	return keys
+}
+
+// Len returns the number of items in the cache.
+func (c *LRU) Len() int {
+	return c.evictList.Len()
+}
+
+// removeOldest removes the oldest item from the cache.
+func (c *LRU) removeOldest() {
+	ent := c.evictList.Back()
+	if ent != nil {
+		c.removeElement(ent)
+	}
+}
+
+// removeElement is used to remove a given list element from the cache
+func (c *LRU) removeElement(e *list.Element) {
+	c.evictList.Remove(e)
+	kv := e.Value.(*entry)
+	delete(c.items, kv.key)
+	if c.onEvict != nil {
+		c.onEvict(kv.key, kv.value)
+	}
+}

+package simplelru
+
+// LRUCache is the interface for simple LRU cache.
+type LRUCache interface {
+	// Adds a value to the cache, returns true if an eviction occurred and
+	// updates the "recently used"-ness of the key.
+	Add(key, value interface{}) bool
+
+	// Returns key's value from the cache and
+	// updates the "recently used"-ness of the key. #value, isFound
+	Get(key interface{}) (value interface{}, ok bool)
+
+	// Check if a key exsists in cache without updating the recent-ness.
+	Contains(key interface{}) (ok bool)
+
+	// Returns key's value without updating the "recently used"-ness of the key.
+	Peek(key interface{}) (value interface{}, ok bool)
+
+	// Removes a key from the cache.
+	Remove(key interface{}) bool
+
+	// Removes the oldest entry from cache.
+	RemoveOldest() (interface{}, interface{}, bool)
+
+	// Returns the oldest entry from the cache. #key, value, isFound
+	GetOldest() (interface{}, interface{}, bool)
+
+	// Returns a slice of the keys in the cache, from oldest to newest.
+	Keys() []interface{}
+
+	// Returns the number of items in the cache.
+	Len() int
+
+	// Clear all cache entries
+	Purge()
+}

+// Package resumption provides primitives for managing network connections
+// that can be interrupted and resumed.
+package resumption
+
+import (
+	"io"
+	"net"
+	"os"
+	"sync"
+	"time"
+)
