+// initialBufSize is the size of the byte buffer backing storage, which is
+// allocated on first use.
+const initialBufSize = 16 * 1024
+
+// byteBuffer is a ring buffer of bytes. Its backing storage is allocated on
+// first use and is never shrunk when data is advanced.
+type byteBuffer struct {
+	// buf is the backing storage.
+	buf []byte
+	// start is the position of the first buffered byte.
+	start int
+	// end is the position one past the last buffered byte.
+	end int
+}
+
+// len returns the number of bytes currently buffered.
+func (b *byteBuffer) len() int {
+	return b.end - b.start
+}
+
+// buffered returns the buffered data as up to two contiguous slices starting
+// at the head of the buffer. When the data wraps around the end of the
+// backing storage, both slices are non-empty, otherwise b2 is empty. The sum
+// of their lengths is equal to len.
+func (b *byteBuffer) buffered() (b1, b2 []byte) {
+	if b.buf == nil || b.end == b.start {
+		return nil, nil
+	}
+	capacity := len(b.buf)
+	s := b.start % capacity
+	e := b.end % capacity
+	if s < e {
+		return b.buf[s:e], nil
+	}
+	// The data wraps around the end of the backing storage (or fills it
+	// entirely, in which case s == e).
+	return b.buf[s:], b.buf[:e]
+}
+
+// free returns the currently unused regions of the buffer, in order, as up to
+// two contiguous slices starting at the tail of the buffer. If the buffer is
+// empty, the two slices together represent the full free space. If the buffer
+// has content, the bounds are calculated and one or two slices representing
+// the unused space are returned. The sum of the lengths of both slices is
+// equal to the total free capacity.
+func (b *byteBuffer) free() (f1, f2 []byte) {
+	if b.buf == nil {
+		b.buf = make([]byte, initialBufSize)
+	}
+	capacity := len(b.buf)
+	if b.end-b.start == capacity {
+		// The buffer is full, there is no free space.
+		return nil, nil
+	}
+	s := b.start % capacity
+	e := b.end % capacity
+	if s <= e {
+		// The buffer is empty or the data is contiguous: the free space is at
+		// both ends of the backing storage.
+		return b.buf[e:], b.buf[:s]
+	}
+	// The data wraps around the end of the backing storage: the free space is
+	// contiguous.
+	return b.buf[e:s], nil
+}
+
+// write appends p to the tail of the buffer without exceeding the maximum
+// allowed buffer size, which is the current capacity of the backing storage.
+// It returns the number of bytes appended, which is zero if the buffer has
+// already reached or surpassed its limit.
+func (b *byteBuffer) write(p []byte) (n int) {
+	if b.buf == nil {
+		b.buf = make([]byte, initialBufSize)
+	}
+	f1, f2 := b.free()
+	n = copy(f1, p)
+	if n < len(p) {
+		n += copy(f2, p[n:])
+	}
+	b.end += n
+	return n
+}
+
+// advance moves the start position of the buffer forward by n, effectively
+// discarding n bytes from the head. If the advancement passes the current
+// end, the end is updated to match the new start, maintaining a consistent
+// empty state. The backing storage is never shrunk.
+func (b *byteBuffer) advance(n int) {
+	if b.buf == nil || n <= 0 {
+		return
+	}
+	b.start += n
+	if b.start > b.end {
+		b.end = b.start
+	}
+}
+
+// read fills p with as much data as available from the buffer, using the
+// result of buffered to perform two copy operations. It advances the buffer
+// by the total number of bytes copied and returns this value.
+func (b *byteBuffer) read(p []byte) (n int) {
+	b1, b2 := b.buffered()
+	n = copy(p, b1)
+	if n < len(p) {
+		n += copy(p[n:], b2)
+	}
+	b.advance(n)
+	return n
+}
+
+// reserve ensures that the buffer has enough free space to accommodate n
+// bytes, reallocating its internal storage if needed. If the current
+// capacity is insufficient, a new capacity is computed by doubling the
+// current one until it meets the requirement, then the storage is
+// reallocated and the existing buffered data is restored.
+func (b *byteBuffer) reserve(n int) {
+	if b.buf == nil {
+		size := initialBufSize
+		for size < n {
+			size *= 2
+		}
+		b.buf = make([]byte, size)
+		return
+	}
+	if len(b.buf)-b.len() >= n {
+		return
+	}
+	size := len(b.buf)
+	for size < b.len()+n {
+		size *= 2
+	}
+	nbuf := make([]byte, size)
+	b1, b2 := b.buffered()
+	copy(nbuf, b1)
+	copy(nbuf[len(b1):], b2)
+	l := b.len()
+	b.buf = nbuf
+	b.start = 0
+	b.end = l
+}
+
+// deadline manages a single deadline with synchronized access.
+type deadline struct {
+	// mu is the mutex that synchronizes access to the deadline state.
+	mu *sync.Mutex
+	// cond is notified when the deadline is reached or the timer is stopped.
+	cond *sync.Cond
+	// timer is the timer that triggers the timeout.
+	timer *time.Timer
+	// timerDone is closed when the callback of the current timer completes.
+	timerDone chan struct{}
+	// timeout is true when the deadline has passed.
+	timeout bool
+	// stopped is true when the timer is initialized but inactive.
+	stopped bool
+	// clock returns the current time.
+	clock func() time.Time
+	// t is the current deadline.
+	t time.Time
+	// hasDeadline is true when a deadline has been set.
+	hasDeadline bool
+}
+
+// now returns the current time according to the deadline's clock.
+func (d *deadline) now() time.Time {
+	if d.clock != nil {
+		return d.clock()
+	}
+	return time.Now()
+}
+
+// broadcastLocked notifies all waiters. The caller must hold d.mu.
+func (d *deadline) broadcastLocked() {
+	if d.cond != nil {
+		d.cond.Broadcast()
+	}
+}
+
+// setDeadlineLocked sets the deadline to t. If t is the zero time, the
+// deadline is cleared. The caller must hold d.mu.
+func (d *deadline) setDeadlineLocked(t time.Time) {
+	// Stop any existing timer, waiting for its callback to complete if
+	// necessary.
+	if d.timer != nil && !d.stopped {
+		if !d.timer.Stop() {
+			<-d.timerDone
+		}
+		d.stopped = true
+	}
+	if t.IsZero() {
+		// Clear the deadline: it is now disabled.
+		d.t = time.Time{}
+		d.hasDeadline = false
+		d.timeout = false
+		d.stopped = true
+		d.broadcastLocked()
+		return
+	}
+	d.t = t
+	d.hasDeadline = true
+	if !t.After(d.now()) {
+		// The deadline is in the past: it has already passed.
+		d.timeout = true
+		d.stopped = true
+		d.broadcastLocked()
+		return
+	}
+	// Schedule a new timer to trigger the timeout and notify waiters when
+	// the deadline is reached.
+	d.timeout = false
+	d.stopped = false
+	d.timerDone = make(chan struct{})
+	done := d.timerDone
+	var timer *time.Timer
+	timer = time.AfterFunc(t.Sub(d.now()), func() {
+		defer close(done)
+		if d.mu != nil {
+			d.mu.Lock()
+			defer d.mu.Unlock()
+		}
+		if d.timerDone == done {
+			d.timeout = true
+			d.stopped = true
+			d.broadcastLocked()
+		}
+	})
+	d.timer = timer
+}
+
+// stopLocked stops the deadline timer. The caller must hold d.mu.
+func (d *deadline) stopLocked() {
+	if d.timer != nil && !d.stopped {
+		if !d.timer.Stop() {
+			<-d.timerDone
+		}
+		d.stopped = true
+	}
+	d.broadcastLocked()
+}
+
+// managedConn is a bidirectional network connection with internal
+// synchronization via a mutex and condition variable. It maintains deadlines,
+// internal buffers for sending and receiving, and flags to track local and
+// remote closure states, allowing safe concurrent access and state aware
+// operations.
+type managedConn struct {
+	// mu protects all fields below.
+	mu sync.Mutex
+	// cond is notified when the state of the connection changes.
+	cond *sync.Cond
+
+	// conn is the underlying connection.
+	conn net.Conn
+
+	// readDeadline is the deadline for Read calls.
+	readDeadline *deadline
+	// writeDeadline is the deadline for Write calls.
+	writeDeadline *deadline
+
+	// in is the buffer of data received from the connection but not yet
+	// returned by Read.
+	in byteBuffer
+	// out is the buffer of data written to the connection but not yet sent.
+	out byteBuffer
+
+	// localClosed is true when Close has been called.
+	localClosed bool
+	// remoteClosed is true when the remote side has closed the connection.
+	remoteClosed bool
+}
+
+// newManagedConn returns a new managedConn wrapping conn, with its condition
+// variable initialized using the associated mutex for synchronization.
+func newManagedConn(conn net.Conn) *managedConn {
+	c := &managedConn{conn: conn}
+	c.cond = sync.NewCond(&c.mu)
+	c.readDeadline = &deadline{mu: &c.mu, cond: c.cond, clock: time.Now}
+	c.writeDeadline = &deadline{mu: &c.mu, cond: c.cond, clock: time.Now}
+	return c
+}
+
+// Close implements the net.Conn interface. It marks the connection as locally
+// closed, stops any active deadline timers, and notifies waiters via the
+// condition variable. If the connection is already closed, it returns
+// net.ErrClosed.
+func (c *managedConn) Close() error {
+	c.mu.Lock()
+	defer c.mu.Unlock()
+	if c.localClosed {
+		return net.ErrClosed
+	}
+	c.localClosed = true
+	c.readDeadline.stopLocked()
+	c.writeDeadline.stopLocked()
+	c.cond.Broadcast()
+	return nil
+}
+
+// Read implements the net.Conn interface. It returns an error if the
+// connection is locally closed or the read deadline has expired. Zero length
+// reads are allowed unconditionally. It returns data when available while
+// notifying waiters, and returns io.EOF if the remote is closed and no data
+// remains.
+func (c *managedConn) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	c.mu.Lock()
+	defer c.mu.Unlock()
+	if len(p) == 0 {
+		return 0, nil
+	}
+	for {
+		if c.localClosed {
+			return 0, net.ErrClosed
+		}
+		if c.readDeadline.timeout {
+			return 0, os.ErrDeadlineExceeded
+		}
+		if n := c.in.read(p); n > 0 {
+			c.cond.Broadcast()
+			return n, nil
+		}
+		if c.remoteClosed {
+			return 0, io.EOF
+		}
+		c.cond.Wait()
+	}
+}
+
+// Write implements the net.Conn interface. It handles concurrent data writes
+// while respecting connection states and deadlines. It returns an error if
+// the connection is locally closed, the write deadline has passed, or the
+// remote side is closed. Zero length inputs are silently accepted.
+func (c *managedConn) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	c.mu.Lock()
+	defer c.mu.Unlock()
+	if len(p) == 0 {
+		return 0, nil
+	}
+	if c.localClosed {
+		return 0, net.ErrClosed
+	}
+	if c.writeDeadline.timeout {
+		return 0, os.ErrDeadlineExceeded
+	}
+	if c.remoteClosed {
+		return 0, net.ErrClosed
+	}
+	c.out.reserve(len(p))
+	n := c.out.write(p)
+	c.cond.Broadcast()
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+// LocalAddr implements the net.Conn interface.
+func (c *managedConn) LocalAddr() net.Addr {
+	return c.conn.LocalAddr()
+}
+
+// RemoteAddr implements the net.Conn interface.
+func (c *managedConn) RemoteAddr() net.Addr {
+	return c.conn.RemoteAddr()
+}
+
+// SetDeadline implements the net.Conn interface.
+func (c *managedConn) SetDeadline(t time.Time) error {
+	c.mu.Lock()
+	defer c.mu.Unlock()
+	c.readDeadline.setDeadlineLocked(t)
+	c.writeDeadline.setDeadlineLocked(t)
+	return nil
+}
+
+// SetReadDeadline implements the net.Conn interface.
+func (c *managedConn) SetReadDeadline(t time.Time) error {
+	c.mu.Lock()
+	defer c.mu.Unlock()
+	c.readDeadline.setDeadlineLocked(t)
+	return nil
+}
+
+// SetWriteDeadline implements the net.Conn interface.
+func (c *managedConn) SetWriteDeadline(t time.Time) error {
+	c.mu.Lock()
+	defer c.mu.Unlock()
+	c.writeDeadline.setDeadlineLocked(t)
+	return nil
+}
+
+// Deadline implements the net.Error interface.
+func (c *managedConn) Deadline() (time.Time, bool) {
+	c.mu.Lock()
+	defer c.mu.Unlock()
+	return c.readDeadline.t, c.readDeadline.hasDeadline
+}

+
+// ClientCertPoolSubjectsLen returns the total size, in bytes, of the CA
+// subjects in pool as they are encoded in a TLS handshake message. Each
+// subject is prefixed with a 2-byte length. Per RFC 5246 section 7.4.4, the
+// total size of the list of acceptable CA subjects must not exceed 2^16-1
+// bytes, otherwise the crypto/tls stack will panic during the handshake.
+func ClientCertPoolSubjectsLen(pool *x509.CertPool) int64 {
+	var total int64
+	for _, subject := range pool.Subjects() {
+		// Each subject in the list gets a separate 2-byte length prefix.
+		total += 2
+		total += int64(len(subject))
+	}
+	return total
+}
+
+// CurrentClusterHostCAPool returns a certificate pool containing only the
+// Host CA of the cluster that client belongs to. It is used as a fallback
+// when the full client certificate pool would be too large to be encoded in
+// a TLS handshake, so that the handshake can still complete.
+func CurrentClusterHostCAPool(client AccessCache) (*x509.CertPool, error) {
+	clusterName, err := client.GetClusterName()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+	hostCA, err := client.GetCertAuthority(
+		services.CertAuthID{Type: services.HostCA, DomainName: clusterName.GetClusterName()},
+		false, services.SkipValidation())
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+	pool := x509.NewCertPool()
+	for _, keyPair := range hostCA.GetTLSKeyPairs() {
+		cert, err := tlsca.ParseCertificatePEM(keyPair.Cert)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+		}
+		log.Debugf("CurrentClusterHostCAPool -> %v", CertInfo(cert))
+		pool.AddCert(cert)
+	}
+	return pool, nil
+}

+package benchmark
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+)
+
+// Config is a single benchmark configuration describing how to run one
+// benchmark at a given rate.
+type Config struct {
+	// Rate is the target rate of requests per second.
+	Rate float64
+	// Threads is the number of threads to run the benchmark with.
+	Threads int
+	// MinimumWindow is the minimum window of measurements.
+	MinimumWindow int
+	// MinimumMeasurements is the minimum number of measurements to take.
+	MinimumMeasurements int
+	// Command is the command to run.
+	Command string
+}
+
+// Linear is a benchmark generator that produces a sequence of benchmark
+// configurations with a linearly increasing rate. It starts at LowerBound,
+// increases by Step on each generation, and stops once the rate would
+// exceed UpperBound.
+type Linear struct {
+	// LowerBound is the lower bound of the rate (requests per second).
+	LowerBound float64
+	// UpperBound is the upper bound of the rate (requests per second).
+	UpperBound float64
+	// Step is the step size by which the rate increases on each generation.
+	Step float64
+	// MinimumMeasurements is the minimum number of measurements to take.
+	MinimumMeasurements int
+	// MinimumWindow is the minimum window of measurements.
+	MinimumWindow int
+	// Threads is the number of threads to run the benchmark with.
+	Threads int
+	// Command is the command to run.
+	Command string
+
+	// rate is the current rate in the linear sequence.
+	rate float64
+}
+
+// GetBenchmark returns the next benchmark configuration in the linear
+// sequence, or nil when the next increment would make the rate strictly
+// greater than UpperBound.
+func (l *Linear) GetBenchmark() *Config {
+	if l.rate < l.LowerBound {
+		l.rate = l.LowerBound
+	}
+	if l.rate > l.UpperBound {
+		return nil
+	}
+	cfg := &Config{
+		Rate:                l.rate,
+		Threads:             l.Threads,
+		MinimumWindow:       l.MinimumWindow,
+		MinimumMeasurements: l.MinimumMeasurements,
+		Command:             l.Command,
+	}
+	l.rate += l.Step
+	return cfg
+}
+
+// validateConfig validates the Linear configuration.
+func validateConfig(l *Linear) error {
+	if l.LowerBound > l.UpperBound {
+		return fmt.Errorf("lower bound %v is greater than upper bound %v", l.LowerBound, l.UpperBound)
+	}
+	if l.MinimumMeasurements == 0 {
+		return fmt.Errorf("minimum measurements must be greater than zero")
+	}
+	return nil
+}

+	// systemUser is the local system user the event is for.
+	systemUser string
+	// teleportUser is the Teleport user the event is for.
+	teleportUser string
+	// address is the address of the client.
+	address string
+	// ttyName is the name of the TTY allocated for the session.
+	ttyName string
+	// dial is a function that creates a netlink connection to the kernel.
+	dial func(family int, config *netlink.Config) (NetlinkConnector, error)
+	// conn is the netlink connection to the kernel, if one is established.
+	conn NetlinkConnector
+}
+
+// NetlinkConnector is an interface abstracting a netlink connection to the
+// Linux kernel.
+type NetlinkConnector interface {
+	// Execute sends a netlink message and returns the response messages.
+	Execute(netlink.Message) ([]netlink.Message, error)
+	// Receive receives netlink messages from the kernel.
+	Receive() ([]netlink.Message, error)
+	// Close closes the netlink connection.
+	Close() error
+}
+
+// NewClient creates a new Client for sending audit events. The client is not
+// connected upon creation; the connection is established lazily when the first
+// event is sent.
+func NewClient(msg Message) *Client {
+	msg.SetDefaults()
+
+	hostname, err := os.Hostname()
+	if err != nil {
+		hostname = UnknownValue
+	}
+
+	return &Client{
+		execName:     filepath.Base(os.Args[0]),
+		hostname:     hostname,
+		systemUser:   msg.SystemUser,
+		teleportUser: msg.TeleportUser,
+		address:      msg.Address,
+		ttyName:      msg.TTYName,
+		dial:         defaultDial,
+	}
+}
+
+// defaultDial creates a netlink connection to the kernel using the default
+// netlink implementation.
+func defaultDial(family int, config *netlink.Config) (NetlinkConnector, error) {
+	return netlink.Dial(family, config)
+}
+
+// SendEvent sends a single audit event to the Linux audit daemon. It is a
+// no-op (returns nil) if auditd is disabled.
+func SendEvent(event EventType, result ResultType, msg Message) error {
+	client := NewClient(msg)
+	err := client.SendMsg(event, result)
+	if errors.Is(err, ErrAuditdDisabled) {
+		return nil
+	}
+	return err
+}
+
+// IsLoginUIDSet checks if the loginuid for the current process is set, which
+// is required for correct audit session tracking.
+func IsLoginUIDSet() bool {
+	uid, err := unix.PrctlRetInt(prGetLoginUID, 0, 0, 0, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	return uint32(uid) != loginUIDUnset
+}
+
+// SendMsg sends a formatted audit message to the audit daemon. It ensures the
+// client is connected and that auditd is enabled before sending the event.
+func (c *Client) SendMsg(event EventType, result ResultType) error {
+	if c.conn == nil {
+		conn, err := c.dial(unix.NETLINK_AUDIT, &netlink.Config{})
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get auditd status: %w", err)
+		}
+		c.conn = conn
+		defer c.Close()
+	}
+
+	// Query the audit status to check if auditd is enabled before emitting
+	// any event.
+	status, err := c.getAuditStatus()
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to get auditd status: %w", err)
+	}
+	if status.Enabled == 0 {
+		return ErrAuditdDisabled
+	}
+
+	// Emit the audit event.
+	return c.sendAuditEvent(event, result)
+}
+
+// Close closes the underlying netlink connection of the auditd client.
+func (c *Client) Close() error {
+	if c.conn == nil {
+		return nil
+	}
+	err := c.conn.Close()
+	c.conn = nil
+	return trace.Wrap(err)
+}
+
+// auditStatus is the audit status returned by the kernel in response to an
+// AUDIT_GET request. It mirrors the kernel's struct audit_status.
+type auditStatus struct {
+	Mask                  int32
+	Enabled               int32
+	Failure               int32
+	Pid                   int32
+	RateLimit             int32
+	BacklogLimit          int32
+	Lost                  int32
+	Backlog               int32
+	FeatureBitmap         int32
+	BacklogWaitTime       int32
+	BacklogWaitTimeActual int32
+}
+
+// getAuditStatus queries the kernel for the current audit status.
+func (c *Client) getAuditStatus() (*auditStatus, error) {
+	// The AUDIT_GET status query has no payload data.
+	msg := netlink.Message{
+		Header: unix.NlMsghdr{
+			Type:  uint16(AuditGet),
+			Flags: unix.NLM_F_REQUEST | unix.NLM_F_ACK,
+		},
+	}
+	responses, err := c.conn.Execute(msg)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+	if len(responses) == 0 {
+		return nil, trace.BadParameter("no response to audit status query")
+	}
+	data := responses[0].Data
+	size := int(unsafe.Sizeof(auditStatus{}))
+	if len(data) < size {
+		return nil, trace.BadParameter("audit status response too short")
+	}
+
+	// Decode the audit status using the platform's native endianness.
+	status := &auditStatus{}
+	order := nativeEndian()
+	status.Mask = int32(order.Uint32(data[0:4]))
+	status.Enabled = int32(order.Uint32(data[4:8]))
+	status.Failure = int32(order.Uint32(data[8:12]))
+	status.Pid = int32(order.Uint32(data[12:16]))
+	status.RateLimit = int32(order.Uint32(data[16:20]))
+	status.BacklogLimit = int32(order.Uint32(data[20:24]))
+	status.Lost = int32(order.Uint32(data[24:28]))
+	status.Backlog = int32(order.Uint32(data[28:32]))
+	status.FeatureBitmap = int32(order.Uint32(data[32:36]))
+	status.BacklogWaitTime = int32(order.Uint32(data[36:40]))
+	status.BacklogWaitTimeActual = int32(order.Uint32(data[40:44]))
+	return status, nil
+}
+
+// sendAuditEvent emits a single audit event to the kernel.
+func (c *Client) sendAuditEvent(event EventType, result ResultType) error {
+	msg := netlink.Message{
+		Header: unix.NlMsghdr{
+			Type:  uint16(event),
+			Flags: unix.NLM_F_REQUEST | unix.NLM_F_ACK,
+		},
+		Data: []byte(c.formatMessage(event, result)),
+	}
+	_, err := c.conn.Execute(msg)
+	return trace.Wrap(err)
+}
+
+// formatMessage formats the audit message payload as space-separated
+// key=value pairs.
+func (c *Client) formatMessage(event EventType, result ResultType) string {
+	msg := fmt.Sprintf("op=%s acct=%q exe=%q hostname=%s addr=%s terminal=%s",
+		c.operation(event), c.systemUser, c.execName, c.hostname, c.address, c.ttyName)
+	if c.teleportUser != "" {
+		msg += fmt.Sprintf(" teleportUser=%s", c.teleportUser)
+	}
+	msg += fmt.Sprintf(" res=%s", c.resultString(result))
+	return msg
+}
+
+// operation returns the "op" field value for the given event type.
+func (c *Client) operation(event EventType) string {
+	switch event {
+	case AuditUserLogin:
+		return "login"
+	case AuditUserEnd:
+		return "session_close"
+	case AuditUserErr:
+		return "invalid_user"
+	}
+	return UnknownValue
+}
+
+// resultString returns the "res" field value for the given result type.
+func (c *Client) resultString(result ResultType) string {
+	switch result {
+	case Success:
+		return "success"
+	case Failed:
+		return "failure"
+	}
+	return UnknownValue
+}
+
+// nativeEndian returns the platform's native byte order.
+func nativeEndian() binary.ByteOrder {
+	var x uint16 = 1
+	if *(*byte)(unsafe.Pointer(&x)) == 1 {
+		return binary.LittleEndian
+	}
+	return binary.BigEndian
+}

+// Package auditd implements a client for the Linux audit daemon (auditd). It
+// is used to report Teleport activity (user logins, session ends, and invalid
+// user/auth failures) to the host's audit pipeline.
+package auditd
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+)
+
+// EventType is the type of an audit event. It corresponds to the kernel audit
+// message type (e.g. AUDIT_USER_LOGIN).
+type EventType = int
+
+// Kernel audit message types.
+const (
+	// AuditGet is the AUDIT_GET message type, used to query the audit status.
+	AuditGet = 0
+	// AuditUserLogin is the AUDIT_USER_LOGIN message type, used to record a
+	// user login.
+	AuditUserLogin = 10
+	// AuditUserEnd is the AUDIT_USER_END message type, used to record the end
+	// of a user session.
+	AuditUserEnd = 11
+	// AuditUserErr is the AUDIT_USER_ERR message type, used to record an
+	// invalid user or authentication failure.
+	AuditUserErr = 12
+)
+
+// ResultType is the result of an audit event.
+type ResultType = int
+
+// Audit event results.
+const (
+	// Success indicates the audit event was successful.
+	Success = 1
+	// Failed indicates the audit event failed.
+	Failed = 0
+)
+
+// UnknownValue is the value used for unknown fields in audit messages,
+// mirroring how OpenSSH represents missing information in its audit logs.
+const UnknownValue = "?"
+
+// ErrAuditdDisabled is returned when the Linux audit daemon is not enabled.
+var ErrAuditdDisabled = errors.New("auditd is disabled")
+
+// Message is the payload of an auditd event.
+type Message struct {
+	// SystemUser is the local system user the event is for.
+	SystemUser string
+	// TeleportUser is the Teleport user the event is for.
+	TeleportUser string
+	// Address is the address of the client.
+	Address string
+	// TTYName is the name of the TTY allocated for the session.
+	TTYName string
+}
+
+// SetDefaults populates empty fields in a Message struct with default values,
+// similar to how OpenSSH handles missing information in its audit logs. The
+// TeleportUser field is intentionally left as-is so that it can be omitted
+// from the audit message when empty.
+func (m *Message) SetDefaults() {
+	if m.SystemUser == "" {
+		m.SystemUser = UnknownValue
+	}
+	if m.Address == "" {
+		m.Address = UnknownValue
+	}
+	if m.TTYName == "" {
+		m.TTYName = UnknownValue
+	}
+}

+// Package netlink provides a minimal implementation of netlink sockets used
+// to communicate with the Linux kernel's audit subsystem.
+package netlink
+
+import (
+	"encoding/binary"
+	"fmt"
+	"unsafe"
+
+	"golang.org/x/sys/unix"
+)
+
+// Message is a netlink message.
+type Message struct {
+	// Header is the netlink message header.
+	Header unix.NlMsghdr
+	// Data is the netlink message payload.
+	Data []byte
+}
+
+// Config is the configuration for a netlink connection.
+type Config struct {
+	// NetNS is a file descriptor for the network namespace to use for the
+	// connection.
+	NetNS int
+}
+
+// Connector is a netlink connection to the Linux kernel.
+type Connector struct {
+	fd       int
+	sequence uint32
+}
+
+// nativeEndian returns the platform's native byte order.
+func nativeEndian() binary.ByteOrder {
+	var x uint16 = 1
+	if *(*byte)(unsafe.Pointer(&x)) == 1 {
+		return binary.LittleEndian
+	}
+	return binary.BigEndian
+}
+
+// Dial creates a new netlink connection bound to the given protocol family.
+func Dial(family int, config *Config) (*Connector, error) {
+	fd, err := unix.Socket(unix.AF_NETLINK, unix.SOCK_RAW, family)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netlink: failed to create socket: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	local := &unix.SockaddrNetlink{
+		Family: unix.AF_NETLINK,
+	}
+	if err := unix.Bind(fd, local); err != nil {
+		unix.Close(fd)
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netlink: failed to bind socket: %w", err)
+	}
+
+	return &Connector{fd: fd}, nil
+}
+
+// Execute sends a netlink message and returns the response messages.
+func (c *Connector) Execute(msg Message) ([]Message, error) {
+	c.sequence++
+	msg.Header.Seq = c.sequence
+	msg.Header.Len = uint32(unix.NLMSG_HDRLEN + len(msg.Data))
+
+	buf, err := serializeMessage(msg)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if err := unix.Send(c.fd, buf, 0); err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netlink: failed to send message: %w", err)
+	}
+	return c.Receive()
+}
+
+// Receive receives netlink messages from the kernel.
+func (c *Connector) Receive() ([]Message, error) {
+	buf := make([]byte, 8192)
+	n, _, err := unix.Recvfrom(c.fd, buf, 0)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("netlink: failed to receive message: %w", err)
+	}
+	return parseMessages(buf[:n])
+}
+
+// Close closes the netlink connection.
+func (c *Connector) Close() error {
+	return unix.Close(c.fd)
+}
+
+// serializeMessage serializes a netlink message into a byte slice.
+func serializeMessage(msg Message) ([]byte, error) {
+	order := nativeEndian()
+	buf := make([]byte, int(msg.Header.Len))
+	order.PutUint32(buf[0:4], msg.Header.Len)
+	order.PutUint16(buf[4:6], msg.Header.Type)
+	order.PutUint16(buf[6:8], msg.Header.Flags)
+	order.PutUint32(buf[8:12], msg.Header.Seq)
+	order.PutUint32(buf[12:16], msg.Header.Pid)
+	copy(buf[unix.NLMSG_HDRLEN:], msg.Data)
+	return buf, nil
+}
+
+// parseMessages parses a byte slice into a list of netlink messages.
+func parseMessages(buf []byte) ([]Message, error) {
+	order := nativeEndian()
+	var messages []Message
+	for len(buf) >= unix.NLMSG_HDRLEN {
+		hdr := unix.NlMsghdr{
+			Len:   order.Uint32(buf[0:4]),
+			Type:  order.Uint16(buf[4:6]),
+			Flags: order.Uint16(buf[6:8]),
+			Seq:   order.Uint32(buf[8:12]),
+			Pid:   order.Uint32(buf[12:16]),
+		}
+		if hdr.Len < unix.NLMSG_HDRLEN || int(hdr.Len) > len(buf) {
+			break
+		}
+		data := make([]byte, int(hdr.Len)-unix.NLMSG_HDRLEN)
+		copy(data, buf[unix.NLMSG_HDRLEN:int(hdr.Len)])
+		messages = append(messages, Message{Header: hdr, Data: data})
+		buf = buf[hdr.Len:]
+	}
+	return messages, nil
+}

+func ReadAtMost(r io.Reader, limit int64) ([]byte, error) {

+//go:build linux

+// Package linux provides utilities for interacting with the Linux system.
+package linux
+
+import (
+	"errors"
+	"io/fs"
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// DMIInfo holds information acquired from the device's DMI.
+type DMIInfo struct {
+	// ProductName is the name of the product.
+	ProductName string
+	// ProductSerial is the serial number of the product.
+	ProductSerial string
+	// BoardSerial is the serial number of the board.
+	BoardSerial string
+	// ChassisAssetTag is the asset tag of the chassis.
+	ChassisAssetTag string
+}
+
+// DMIInfoFromSysfs reads DMI information from /sys/class/dmi/id.
+func DMIInfoFromSysfs() (*DMIInfo, error) {
+	return DMIInfoFromFS(os.DirFS("/sys/class/dmi/id"))
+}
+
+// DMIInfoFromFS reads DMI information from the given filesystem. It always
+// returns a non-nil DMIInfo, with errors from any failed reads joined
+// together.
+func DMIInfoFromFS(dmifs fs.FS) (*DMIInfo, error) {
+	dmiInfo := &DMIInfo{}
+	var errs []error
+
+	read := func(path string, dst *string) {
+		b, err := fs.ReadFile(dmifs, path)
+		if err != nil {
+			errs = append(errs, err)
+			return
+		}
+		*dst = strings.TrimSpace(string(b))
+	}
+
+	read("product_name", &dmiInfo.ProductName)
+	read("product_serial", &dmiInfo.ProductSerial)
+	read("board_serial", &dmiInfo.BoardSerial)
+	read("chassis_asset_tag", &dmiInfo.ChassisAssetTag)
+
+	return dmiInfo, errors.Join(errs...)
+}

+//go:build linux
+
+package linux
+
+import (
+	"bufio"
+	"io"
+	"os"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/trace"
+)
+
+// OSRelease represents the parsed contents of the /etc/os-release file.
+type OSRelease struct {
+	// PrettyName is the pretty name of the OS.
+	PrettyName string
+	// Name is the name of the OS.
+	Name string
+	// VersionID is the version ID of the OS.
+	VersionID string
+	// Version is the version of the OS.
+	Version string
+	// ID is the ID of the OS.
+	ID string
+}
+
+// ParseOSRelease parses the /etc/os-release file.
+func ParseOSRelease() (*OSRelease, error) {
+	f, err := os.Open("/etc/os-release")
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+	defer f.Close()
+
+	return ParseOSReleaseFromReader(f)
+}
+
+// ParseOSReleaseFromReader parses the contents of an os-release file from the
+// given reader. Lines that do not conform to the key=value format are
+// ignored. Quotes surrounding values are trimmed.
+func ParseOSReleaseFromReader(in io.Reader) (*OSRelease, error) {
+	osRelease := &OSRelease{}
+	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(in)
+	for scanner.Scan() {
+		line := scanner.Text()
+		parts := strings.Split(line, "=")
+		if len(parts) != 2 {
+			continue
+		}
+		key := parts[0]
+		value := strings.Trim(parts[1], `"'`)
+		switch key {
+		case "PRETTY_NAME":
+			osRelease.PrettyName = value
+		case "NAME":
+			osRelease.Name = value
+		case "VERSION_ID":
+			osRelease.VersionID = value
+		case "VERSION":
+			osRelease.Version = value
+		case "ID":
+			osRelease.ID = value
+		}
+	}
+	if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
+		return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+
+	return osRelease, nil
+}

+// Package keystore provides an abstraction for managing cryptographic keys.
+package keystore
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"crypto"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport/api/types"
+
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"
+)
+
+// KeyStore is an interface for managing cryptographic keys.
+type KeyStore interface {
+	// GenerateKey generates a new RSA key and returns the key identifier
+	// and a signer for it.
+	GenerateKey() (string, crypto.Signer, error)
+
+	// GetSigner returns a signer for the key with the given identifier.
+	GetSigner(keyID string) (crypto.Signer, error)
+
+	// DeleteKey deletes the key with the given identifier.
+	DeleteKey(keyID string) error
+
+	// SelectSSHKey selects a key to use for signing SSH certificates from
+	// the given certificate authority.
+	SelectSSHKey(ca types.CertAuthority) (ssh.Signer, error)
+
+	// SelectTLSKey selects a key to use for signing TLS certificates from
+	// the given certificate authority.
+	SelectTLSKey(ca types.CertAuthority) ([][]byte, crypto.Signer, error)
+
+	// SelectJWTKey selects a key to use for signing JWTs from the given
+	// certificate authority.
+	SelectJWTKey(ca types.CertAuthority) (crypto.Signer, error)
+}
+
+// KeyType returns the type of the private key in the given bytes.
+func KeyType(key []byte) types.PrivateKeyType {
+	if bytes.HasPrefix(key, []byte("pkcs11:")) {
+		return types.PrivateKeyType_PKCS11
+	}
+	return types.PrivateKeyType_RAW
+}
diff --git a/lib/auth/keystore/raw.go b/lib/auth/keystore/raw.go
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..4e19484a5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/lib/auth/keystore/raw.go
@@ -0,0 +1,182 @@
+/*
+Copyright 2021 Gravitational, Inc.
+
+Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+You may obtain a copy of the License at
+
+    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+
+Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
+distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
+WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+limitations under the License.
+*/
+
+package keystore
+
+import (
+	"crypto"
+	"crypto/rand"
+	"crypto/rsa"
+	"crypto/sha256"
+	"crypto/x509"
+	"encoding/hex"
+	"encoding/pem"
+	"sync"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport"
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport/api/types"
+	"github.com/gravitational/teleport/lib/utils"
+
+	"github.com/gravitational/trace"
+	"golang.org/x/crypto/ssh"
+)
+
+// RSAKeyPairSource is a function that generates an RSA key pair.
+type RSAKeyPairSource func(name string) (priv []byte, pub []byte, err error)
+
+// RawConfig holds the configuration for a rawKeyStore.
+type RawConfig struct {
+	// RSAKeyPairSource is a function that generates an RSA key pair.
+	RSAKeyPairSource RSAKeyPairSource
+}
+
+// NewRawKeyStore returns a new rawKeyStore.
+func NewRawKeyStore(config *RawConfig) KeyStore {
+	if config == nil {
+		config = &RawConfig{}
+	}
+	if config.RSAKeyPairSource == nil {
+		config.RSAKeyPairSource = generateKeyPair
+	}
+	return &rawKeyStore{
+		config: config,
+		keys:   make(map[string]*rsa.PrivateKey),
+	}
+}
+
+// generateKeyPair generates a new RSA key pair and returns the private and
+// public keys in PEM format.
+func generateKeyPair(name string) (priv []byte, pub []byte, err error) {
+	key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, teleport.RSAKeySize)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+	priv = pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{
+		Type:  "RSA PRIVATE KEY",
+		Bytes: x509.MarshalPKCS1PrivateKey(key),
+	})
+	pub = pem.EncodeToMemory(&pem.Block{
+		Type:  "RSA PUBLIC KEY",
+		Bytes: x509.MarshalPKCS1PublicKey(&key.PublicKey),
+	})
+	return priv, pub, nil
+}
+
+// rawKeyStore is a KeyStore that stores keys in raw PEM format.
+type rawKeyStore struct {
+	mu     sync.Mutex
+	config *RawConfig
+	keys   map[string]*rsa.PrivateKey
+}
+
+// GenerateKey generates a new RSA key and returns the key identifier and
+// a signer for it.
+func (k *rawKeyStore) GenerateKey() (string, crypto.Signer, error) {
+	priv, _, err := k.config.RSAKeyPairSource("rsa")
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+
+	key, err := utils.ParsePrivateKeyPEM(priv)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+	}
+
+	rsaKey, ok := key.(*rsa.PrivateKey)
+	if !ok {
+		return "", nil, trace.BadParameter("expected *rsa.PrivateKey, got %T", key)
+	}
+
+	sum := sha256.Sum256(rsaKey.PublicKey.N.Bytes())
+	keyID := hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
+
+	k.mu.Lock()
+	k.keys[keyID] = rsaKey
+	k.mu.Unlock()
+
+	return keyID, rsaKey, nil
+}
+
+// GetSigner returns a signer for the key with the given identifier.
+func (k *rawKeyStore) GetSigner(keyID string) (crypto.Signer, error) {
+	k.mu.Lock()
+	defer k.mu.Unlock()
+
+	key, ok := k.keys[keyID]
+	if !ok {
+		return nil, trace.NotFound("key %q not found", keyID)
+	}
+	return key, nil
+}
+
+// DeleteKey deletes the key with the given identifier.
+func (k *rawKeyStore) DeleteKey(keyID string) error {
+	return nil
+}
+
+// SelectSSHKey selects a key to use for signing SSH certificates from
+// the given certificate authority.
+func (k *rawKeyStore) SelectSSHKey(ca types.CertAuthority) (ssh.Signer, error) {
+	for _, keySet := range []types.CAKeySet{ca.GetActiveKeys(), ca.GetAdditionalTrustedKeys()} {
+		for _, kp := range keySet.SSH {
+			if kp == nil || KeyType(kp.PrivateKey) != types.PrivateKeyType_RAW {
+				continue
+			}
+			signer, err := ssh.ParsePrivateKey(kp.PrivateKey)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+			}
+			return signer, nil
+		}
+	}
+	return nil, trace.NotFound("no RAW SSH key found in %v", ca)
+}
+
+// SelectTLSKey selects a key to use for signing TLS certificates from
+// the given certificate authority.
+func (k *rawKeyStore) SelectTLSKey(ca types.CertAuthority) ([][]byte, crypto.Signer, error) {
+	for _, keySet := range []types.CAKeySet{ca.GetActiveKeys(), ca.GetAdditionalTrustedKeys()} {
+		for _, kp := range keySet.TLS {
+			if kp == nil || KeyType(kp.Key) != types.PrivateKeyType_RAW {
+				continue
+			}
+			signer, err := utils.ParsePrivateKeyPEM(kp.Key)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+			}
+			return [][]byte{kp.Cert}, signer, nil
+		}
+	}
+	return nil, nil, trace.NotFound("no RAW TLS key found in %v", ca)
+}
+
+// SelectJWTKey selects a key to use for signing JWTs from the given
+// certificate authority.
+func (k *rawKeyStore) SelectJWTKey(ca types.CertAuthority) (crypto.Signer, error) {
+	for _, keySet := range []types.CAKeySet{ca.GetActiveKeys(), ca.GetAdditionalTrustedKeys()} {
+		for _, kp := range keySet.JWT {
+			if kp == nil || KeyType(kp.PrivateKey) != types.PrivateKeyType_RAW {
+				continue
+			}
+			signer, err := utils.ParsePrivateKeyPEM(kp.PrivateKey)
+			if err != nil {
+				return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
+			}
+			return signer, nil
+		}
+	}
+	return nil, trace.NotFound("no RAW JWT key found in %v", ca)
+}

--- /dev/null
+++ b/openlibrary/solr/utils.py
@@ -0,0 +1,199 @@
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+import json
+import logging
+
+import httpx
+
+from httpx import HTTPError, HTTPStatusError, TimeoutException
+
+from openlibrary import config
+from openlibrary.solr.solr_types import SolrDocument
+from openlibrary.utils.retry import MaxRetriesExceeded, RetryStrategy
+
+logger = logging.getLogger("openlibrary.solr")
+
+solr_base_url = None
+solr_next: bool | None = None
+
+
+def get_solr_base_url():
+    """
+    Get Solr host
+
+    :rtype: str
+    """
+    global solr_base_url
+
+    load_config()
+
+    if not solr_base_url:
+        solr_base_url = config.runtime_config['plugin_worksearch']['solr_base_url']
+
+    return solr_base_url
+
+
+def set_solr_base_url(solr_url: str):
+    global solr_base_url
+    solr_base_url = solr_url
+
+
+def get_solr_next() -> bool:
+    """
+    Get whether this is the next version of solr; ie new schema configs/fields, etc.
+    """
+    global solr_next
+
+    if solr_next is None:
+        load_config()
+        solr_next = config.runtime_config['plugin_worksearch'].get('solr_next', False)
+
+    return solr_next
+
+
+def set_solr_next(val: bool):
+    global solr_next
+    solr_next = val
+
+
+def load_config(c_config='conf/openlibrary.yml'):
+    if not config.runtime_config:
+        config.load(c_config)
+        config.load_config(c_config)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SolrUpdateState:
+    keys: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    """Keys to update"""
+
+    adds: list[SolrDocument] = field(default_factory=list)
+    """Records to be added/modified"""
+
+    deletes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    """Records to be deleted"""
+
+    commit: bool = False
+
+    # Override the + operator
+    def __add__(self, other):
+        if isinstance(other, SolrUpdateState):
+            return SolrUpdateState(
+                adds=self.adds + other.adds,
+                deletes=self.deletes + other.deletes,
+                keys=self.keys + other.keys,
+                commit=self.commit or other.commit,
+            )
+        else:
+            raise TypeError(f"Cannot add {type(self)} and {type(other)}")
+
+    def has_changes(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self.adds or self.deletes)
+
+    def to_solr_requests_json(self, indent: str | None = None, sep=',') -> str:
+        result = '{'
+        if self.deletes:
+            result += f'"delete": {json.dumps(self.deletes, indent=indent)}' + sep
+        for doc in self.adds:
+            result += f'"add": {json.dumps({"doc": doc}, indent=indent)}' + sep
+        if self.commit:
+            result += '"commit": {}' + sep
+
+        if result.endswith(sep):
+            result = result[: -len(sep)]
+        result += '}'
+        return result
+
+    def clear_requests(self) -> None:
+        self.adds.clear()
+        self.deletes.clear()
+
+
+async def solr_insert_documents(
+    documents: list[dict],
+    solr_base_url: str | None = None,
+    skip_id_check=False,
+):
+    """
+    Note: This has only been tested with Solr 8, but might work with Solr 3 as well.
+    """
+    solr_base_url = solr_base_url or get_solr_base_url()
+    params = {}
+    if skip_id_check:
+        params['overwrite'] = 'false'
+    logger.debug(f"POSTing update to {solr_base_url}/update {params}")
+    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
+        resp = await client.post(
+            f'{solr_base_url}/update',
+            timeout=30,  # seconds; the default timeout is silly short
+            params=params,
+            headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
+            content=json.dumps(documents),
+        )
+    resp.raise_for_status()
+
+
+def solr_update(
+    update_request: SolrUpdateState,
+    skip_id_check=False,
+    solr_base_url: str | None = None,
+) -> None:
+    content = update_request.to_solr_requests_json()
+
+    solr_base_url = solr_base_url or get_solr_base_url()
+    params = {
+        # Don't fail the whole batch if one bad apple
+        'update.chain': 'tolerant-chain'
+    }
+    if skip_id_check:
+        params['overwrite'] = 'false'
+
+    def make_request():
+        logger.debug(f"POSTing update to {solr_base_url}/update {params}")
+        try:
+            resp = httpx.post(
+                f'{solr_base_url}/update',
+                # Large batches especially can take a decent chunk of time
+                timeout=300,
+                params=params,
+                headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
+                content=content,
+            )
+
+            if resp.status_code == 400:
+                resp_json = resp.json()
+
+                indiv_errors = resp_json.get('responseHeader', {}).get('errors', [])
+                if indiv_errors:
+                    for e in indiv_errors:
+                        logger.error(f'Individual Solr POST Error: {e}')
+
+                global_error = resp_json.get('error')
+                if global_error:
+                    logger.error(f'Global Solr POST Error: {global_error.get("msg")}')
+
+                if not (indiv_errors or global_error):
+                    # We can handle the above errors. Any other 400 status codes
+                    # are fatal and should cause a retry
+                    resp.raise_for_status()
+            else:
+                resp.raise_for_status()
+        except HTTPStatusError as e:
+            logger.error(f'HTTP Status Solr POST Error: {e}')
+            raise
+        except TimeoutException:
+            logger.error(f'Timeout Solr POST Error: {content}')
+            raise
+        except HTTPError as e:
+            logger.error(f'HTTP Solr POST Error: {e}')
+            raise
+
+    retry = RetryStrategy(
+        [HTTPStatusError, TimeoutException, HTTPError],
+        max_retries=5,
+        delay=8,
+    )
+
+    try:
+        return retry(make_request)
+    except MaxRetriesExceeded as e:
+        logger.error(f'Max retries exceeded for Solr POST: {e.last_exception}')

+def make_date_string(

@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python
+"""
+To run:
+
+PYTHONPATH=. python ./scripts/import_open_textbook_library.py /olsystem/etc/openlibrary.yml
+"""
+
+import json
+import time
+from typing import Any, Generator
+
+import requests
+
+from openlibrary.config import load_config
+from openlibrary.core.imports import Batch
+from scripts.solr_builder.solr_builder.fn_to_cli import FnToCLI
+
+FEED_URL = 'https://opentextbookstore.com/api/v1/textbooks.json'
+
+
+def get_feed() -> Generator[dict[str, Any], None, None]:
+    """Fetches and yields each textbook in the Open Textbook Library feed."""
+    url = FEED_URL
+    while url:
+        r = requests.get(url)
+        data = r.json()
+        for textbook in data['data']:
+            yield textbook
+        url = data['links'].get('next')
+
+
+def map_data(data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Maps Open Textbook Library data to an Open Library import object."""
+    import_record = {
+        'identifiers': {'open_textbook_library': str(data['id'])},
+        'source_records': [f'open_textbook_library:{data["id"]}'],
+        'title': data['title'],
+    }
+
+    if data.get('isbn_10'):
+        import_record['isbn_10'] = [data['isbn_10']]
+    if data.get('isbn_13'):
+        import_record['isbn_13'] = [data['isbn_13']]
+    if data.get('language'):
+        import_record['languages'] = [data['language']]
+    if data.get('description'):
+        import_record['description'] = data['description']
+
+    authors = []
+    contributions = []
+    for contributor in data.get('contributors') or []:
+        name = ' '.join(
+            filter(
+                None,
+                [
+                    contributor.get('first_name'),
+                    contributor.get('middle_name'),
+                    contributor.get('last_name'),
+                ],
+            )
+        )
+        if contributor.get('primary') or contributor.get('role') == 'Authors':
+            authors.append({'name': name})
+        else:
+            contributions.append(name)
+    if authors:
+        import_record['authors'] = authors
+    if contributions:
+        import_record['contributions'] = contributions
+
+    subjects = []
+    lc_classifications = []
+    for subject in data.get('subjects') or []:
+        if subject.get('name'):
+            subjects.append(subject['name'])
+        if subject.get('lc_call_number'):
+            lc_classifications.append(subject['lc_call_number'])
+    if subjects:
+        import_record['subjects'] = subjects
+    if lc_classifications:
+        import_record['lc_classifications'] = lc_classifications
+
+    if data.get('publisher'):
+        import_record['publishers'] = [data['publisher']['name']]
+    if data.get('copyright_year'):
+        import_record['publish_date'] = str(data['copyright_year'])
+
+    return import_record
+
+
+def create_import_jobs(records: list[dict[str, str]]) -> None:
+    """Creates Open Textbook Library batch import job.
+
+    Attempts to find existing Open Textbook Library import batch.
+    If nothing is found, a new batch is created. All of the
+    given import records are added to the batch job as JSON strings.
+    """
+    now = time.gmtime(time.time())
+    batch_name = f'open_textbook_library-{now.tm_year}{now.tm_mon}'
+    batch = Batch.find(batch_name) or Batch.new(batch_name)
+    batch.add_items([{'ia_id': r['source_records'][0], 'data': r} for r in records])
+
+
+def import_job(ol_config: str, dry_run: bool = False, limit: int = 10) -> None:
+    """
+    :param str ol_config: Path to openlibrary.yml file
+    :param bool dry_run: If true, only print out records to import
+    :param int limit: Number of records to import
+    """
+    load_config(ol_config)
+
+    # Get feed:
+    d = get_feed()
+
+    # Map feed entries to list of import objects:
+    print('Importing Open Textbook Library entries.')
+    entries = [map_data(e) for e in d]
+
+    if limit is not None:
+        entries = entries[:limit]
+
+    if not dry_run:
+        create_import_jobs(entries)
+        print(f'{len(entries)} entries added to the batch import job.')
+    else:
+        for record in entries:
+            print(json.dumps(record))
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    print('Start: Open Textbook Library import job')
+    FnToCLI(import_job).run()
+    print('End: Open Textbook Library import job')

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/mime/mime.go
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+package mime
+
+import (
+	_ "embed"
+	"fmt"
+	"mime"
+	"sort"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/conf"
+	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/log"
+	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
+)
+
+//go:embed mime_types.yaml
+var mimeTypesYAML []byte
+
+type MimeType struct {
+	Types    map[string]string `yaml:"types"`
+	Lossless []string          `yaml:"lossless"`
+}
+
+var LosslessFormats []string
+
+func init() {
+	conf.AddHook(func() {
+		if err := load(); err != nil {
+			log.Error("Error loading mime types", "error", err)
+		}
+	})
+}
+
+func load() error {
+	var mimeTypes MimeType
+	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(mimeTypesYAML, &mimeTypes); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("error unmarshaling mime types: %w", err)
+	}
+	for ext, typ := range mimeTypes.Types {
+		_ = mime.AddExtensionType(ext, typ)
+	}
+	LosslessFormats = make([]string, 0, len(mimeTypes.Lossless))
+	for _, ext := range mimeTypes.Lossless {
+		LosslessFormats = append(LosslessFormats, strings.TrimPrefix(ext, "."))
+	}
+	sort.Strings(LosslessFormats)
+
+	// In some circumstances, Windows sets JS mime-type to `text/plain`!
+	_ = mime.AddExtensionType(".js", "text/javascript")
+	_ = mime.AddExtensionType(".css", "text/css")
+	return nil
+}

new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..f03ec86a83
--- /dev/null
+++ b/applications/drive/src/app/utils/replaceLocalURL.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+/**
+ * Utility module for local development environments using the local-sso proxy configuration.
+ *
+ * When the application is served from a `*.proton.local` host (local-sso environment),
+ * service URLs generated against the `*.proton.black` domain are not compatible with the
+ * local proxy. Such URLs must be rewritten to the equivalent `*.proton.local` host (using
+ * the current page's port) so that requests go through the same local proxy. In all other
+ * environments (e.g. `localhost`, `proton.me`) URLs are returned unchanged.
+ */
+
+const PROTON_BLACK_HOST = 'proton.black';
+const PROTON_LOCAL_HOST = 'proton.local';
+
+/**
+ * Whether a host is the `proton.local` base host or a `*.proton.local` subdomain.
+ */
+const isProtonLocalHost = (host: string): boolean => host === PROTON_LOCAL_HOST || host.endsWith(`.${PROTON_LOCAL_HOST}`);
+
+/**
+ * Whether a host is the `proton.black` base host or a `*.proton.black` subdomain.
+ */
+const isProtonBlackHost = (host: string): boolean => host === PROTON_BLACK_HOST || host.endsWith(`.${PROTON_BLACK_HOST}`);
+
+/**
+ * Rewrite a URL so it works with the local-sso proxy.
+ *
+ * Only active when the current browser hostname ends with `proton.local`: URLs whose host
+ * is `proton.black` or a `*.proton.black` subdomain are rewritten to the corresponding
+ * `proton.local` host, keeping the current page's port. The leftmost label of the input
+ * hostname is used as the service identifier (e.g. `drive.env.proton.black` becomes
+ * `drive.proton.local`, `drive-api.proton.black` becomes `drive-api.proton.local`), so
+ * environment labels and hyphens are handled correctly.
+ *
+ * The original scheme, path, query parameters and fragment are preserved. URLs already
+ * targeting `proton.local` (with or without a port) are returned without modification,
+ * and in non-local environments the input URL is returned unchanged.
+ *
+ * @param href - Absolute URL to transform.
+ * @returns The rewritten URL, or the original URL when no rewrite applies.
+ * @throws {TypeError} If `href` is not a valid absolute URL.
+ */
+export const replaceLocalURL = (href: string): string => {
+    // Throws the standard TypeError if `href` is not a valid absolute URL.
+    const url = new URL(href);
+
+    const { hostname: currentHostname, port: currentPort } = window.location;
+
+    // Only rewrite in local-sso environments; leave all other environments unchanged.
+    if (!isProtonLocalHost(currentHostname)) {
+        return href;
+    }
+
+    // Idempotence: URLs already targeting proton.local are returned without modification.
+    if (isProtonLocalHost(url.hostname)) {
+        return href;
+    }
+
+    // Only rewrite URLs pointing to the proton.black domain.
+    if (!isProtonBlackHost(url.hostname)) {
+        return href;
+    }
+
+    // The leftmost label of the hostname identifies the service (e.g. `drive`, `drive-api`).
+    const service = url.hostname.split('.')[0];
+    url.hostname = service === PROTON_BLACK_HOST.split('.')[0] ? PROTON_LOCAL_HOST : `${service}.${PROTON_LOCAL_HOST}`;
+
+    // Apply the current page's port (clearing it when the page uses the default port).
+    url.port = currentPort;
+
+    return url.href;
+};

+"""A best-effort, simplistic parser for ELF files.
+
+This is used to find the version of QtWebEngineCore in the ELF file, as the
+user agent string can be modified by the user.
+"""
+
+import os
+import re
+import sys
+import mmap
+import enum
+import glob
+import struct
+import dataclasses
+from typing import IO, List
+
+from PyQt5.QtCore import QLibraryInfo
+
+
+class ParseError(Exception):
+
+    """Raised on ELF parsing errors."""
+
+
+class Bitness(enum.Enum):
+
+    """Bitness of the ELF file."""
+
+    elf32 = 1
+    elf64 = 2
+
+
+class Endianness(enum.Enum):
+
+    """Endianness of the ELF file."""
+
+    little = 1
+    big = 2
+
+
+def _endianness_prefix() -> str:
+    """Get the struct format prefix for the host endianness."""
+    return '<' if sys.byteorder == 'little' else '>'
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class Ident:
+
+    """ELF identification header.
+
+    See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executable_and_Linkable_Format#File_format
+    """
+
+    magic: bytes
+    bitness: Bitness
+    endianness: Endianness
+    version: int
+    osabi: int
+    abiversion: int
+    pad: bytes
+
+    @classmethod
+    def parse(cls, fobj: IO[bytes]) -> 'Ident':
+        """Parse an ELF identification from a file object."""
+        data = fobj.read(16)
+        if len(data) < 16:
+            raise ParseError("File too short to be an ELF")
+
+        magic = data[:4]
+        if magic != b'\x7fELF':
+            raise ParseError(f"Bad magic: {magic!r}")
+
+        bitness_raw = data[4]
+        if bitness_raw == 1:
+            bitness = Bitness.elf32
+        elif bitness_raw == 2:
+            bitness = Bitness.elf64
+        else:
+            raise ParseError(f"Unsupported bitness: {bitness_raw}")
+
+        endianness_raw = data[5]
+        if endianness_raw == 1:
+            endianness = Endianness.little
+        elif endianness_raw == 2:
+            endianness = Endianness.big
+        else:
+            raise ParseError(f"Unsupported endianness: {endianness_raw}")
+
+        version = data[6]
+        if version != 1:
+            raise ParseError(f"Unsupported ELF version: {version}")
+
+        osabi = data[7]
+        abiversion = data[8]
+        pad = data[9:16]
+
+        return cls(magic=magic, bitness=bitness, endianness=endianness,
+                   version=version, osabi=osabi, abiversion=abiversion,
+                   pad=pad)
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class Header:
+
+    """ELF header.
+
+    See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executable_and_Linkable_Format#File_format
+    """
+
+    type: int
+    machine: int
+    version: int
+    entry: int
+    phoff: int
+    shoff: int
+    flags: int
+    ehsize: int
+    phentsize: int
+    phnum: int
+    shentsize: int
+    shnum: int
+    shstrndx: int
+
+    @classmethod
+    def parse(cls, fobj: IO[bytes], bitness: Bitness) -> 'Header':
+        """Parse an ELF header from a file object.
+
+        The file object must be positioned right after the ELF
+        identification.
+        """
+        if bitness == Bitness.elf32:
+            fmt = 'HHIIIIIHHHHHH'
+        elif bitness == Bitness.elf64:
+            fmt = 'HHIQQQIHHHHHH'
+        else:
+            raise ParseError(f"Unsupported bitness: {bitness}")
+
+        fmt = _endianness_prefix() + fmt
+        size = struct.calcsize(fmt)
+        data = fobj.read(size)
+        if len(data) < size:
+            raise ParseError("File too short to be an ELF")
+
+        (type_, machine, version, entry, phoff, shoff, flags,
+         ehsize, phentsize, phnum, shentsize, shnum, shstrndx) = struct.unpack(fmt, data)
+
+        if version != 1:
+            raise ParseError(f"Unsupported ELF version: {version}")
+
+        return cls(type=type_, machine=machine, version=version, entry=entry,
+                   phoff=phoff, shoff=shoff, flags=flags, ehsize=ehsize,
+                   phentsize=phentsize, phnum=phnum, shentsize=shentsize,
+                   shnum=shnum, shstrndx=shstrndx)
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class SectionHeader:
+
+    """ELF section header.
+
+    See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executable_and_Linkable_Format#File_format
+    """
+
+    name_offset: int
+    type: int
+    flags: int
+    addr: int
+    offset: int
+    size: int
+    link: int
+    info: int
+    addralign: int
+    entsize: int
+
+    @classmethod
+    def parse(cls, fobj: IO[bytes], bitness: Bitness) -> 'SectionHeader':
+        """Parse an ELF section header from a file object."""
+        if bitness == Bitness.elf32:
+            fmt = 'IIIIIIIIII'
+        elif bitness == Bitness.elf64:
+            fmt = 'IIQQQQIIQQ'
+        else:
+            raise ParseError(f"Unsupported bitness: {bitness}")
+
+        fmt = _endianness_prefix() + fmt
+        size = struct.calcsize(fmt)
+        data = fobj.read(size)
+        if len(data) < size:
+            raise ParseError("File too short to be an ELF")
+
+        (name_offset, type_, flags, addr, offset, size_, link, info,
+         addralign, entsize) = struct.unpack(fmt, data)
+
+        return cls(name_offset=name_offset, type=type_, flags=flags,
+                   addr=addr, offset=offset, size=size_, link=link,
+                   info=info, addralign=addralign, entsize=entsize)
+
+
+@dataclasses.dataclass
+class Versions:
+
+    """The versions of QtWebEngine and Chromium found in an ELF file."""
+
+    webengine: str
+    chromium: str
+
+
+def _get_string(data: bytes, offset: int) -> str:
+    """Get a NUL-terminated string from data at a given offset.
+
+    Raise:
+        ParseError: If the string can't be found or decoded.
+    """
+    if offset >= len(data):
+        raise ParseError(f"String offset {offset} out of bounds")
+    end = data.find(b'\0', offset)
+    if end == -1:
+        end = len(data)
+    try:
+        return data[offset:end].decode('ascii')
+    except UnicodeDecodeError as e:
+        raise ParseError(f"Failed to decode string: {e}")
+
+
+def get_rodata_header(fobj: IO[bytes]) -> SectionHeader:
+    """Find the .rodata section header of an ELF file.
+
+    Args:
+        fobj: A file object positioned at the start of the ELF file.
+
+    Return:
+        The SectionHeader of the .rodata section.
+
+    Raise:
+        ParseError: If the file is not a valid ELF file or doesn't have a
+                    .rodata section.
+    """
+    ident = Ident.parse(fobj)
+    header = Header.parse(fobj, ident.bitness)
+
+    fobj.seek(header.shoff)
+    section_headers: List[SectionHeader] = []
+    for _ in range(header.shnum):
+        section_headers.append(SectionHeader.parse(fobj, ident.bitness))
+
+    if not 0 <= header.shstrndx < len(section_headers):
+        raise ParseError(f"Invalid shstrndx: {header.shstrndx}")
+    shstrtab = section_headers[header.shstrndx]
+    fobj.seek(shstrtab.offset)
+    shstrtab_data = fobj.read(shstrtab.size)
+
+    for sh in section_headers:
+        if _get_string(shstrtab_data, sh.name_offset) == '.rodata':
+            return sh
+
+    raise ParseError("No .rodata section found")
+
+
+def get_rodata(path: str) -> bytes:
+    """Get the .rodata section of an ELF file.
+
+    Args:
+        path: The path to the ELF file.
+
+    Return:
+        The contents of the .rodata section.
+
+    Raise:
+        ParseError: If the file is not a valid ELF file or doesn't have a
+                    .rodata section.
+    """
+    try:
+        with open(path, 'rb') as f:
+            fobj = mmap.mmap(f.fileno(), 0, prot=mmap.PROT_READ)
+            try:
+                header = get_rodata_header(fobj)
+                fobj.seek(header.offset)
+                return fobj.read(header.size)
+            finally:
+                fobj.close()
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
+        raise ParseError(f"Failed to read {path}: {e}")
+
+
+def _get_webenginecore_path() -> str:
+    """Find the path to the QtWebEngineCore library.
+
+    Raise:
+        ParseError: If the library could not be found.
+    """
+    libdir = QLibraryInfo.location(QLibraryInfo.LibrariesPath)
+    matches = glob.glob(os.path.join(libdir, 'libQt5WebEngineCore.so.5*'))
+    if not matches:
+        raise ParseError(f"libQt5WebEngineCore.so.5 not found in {libdir}")
+    return matches[0]
+
+
+def parse_webenginecore() -> Versions:
+    """Parse the QtWebEngineCore library to find its version.
+
+    Return:
+        A Versions object.
+
+    Raise:
+        ParseError: If the library could not be found or parsed.
+    """
+    path = _get_webenginecore_path()
+    data = get_rodata(path)
+
+    webengine_match = re.search(rb'QtWebEngine/([0-9.]+)', data)
+    if webengine_match is None:
+        raise ParseError("QtWebEngine version not found in ELF")
+    chromium_match = re.search(rb'Chrome/([0-9.]+)', data)
+    if chromium_match is None:
+        raise ParseError("Chromium version not found in ELF")
+
+    return Versions(webengine=webengine_match.group(1).decode('ascii'),
+                    chromium=chromium_match.group(1).decode('ascii'))

+/**
+ * Normalizes a contact social media id into a full url.
+ * If the value already contains a scheme ("http") or "www." it is returned as-is (trimmed).
+ * Known social media types are mapped to their standard base paths, for other or custom sites
+ * only "https://" (and "www.") is prepended without appending a site-specific path.
+ */
+export function getSocialUrl(contactSocialId: ContactSocialId): string {
+	const socialId = contactSocialId.socialId.trim()
+
+	if (socialId.indexOf("http") !== -1 || socialId.indexOf("www.") !== -1) {
+		return socialId
+	}
+
+	let socialUrlType = ""
+	switch (contactSocialId.type) {
+		case ContactSocialType.TWITTER:
+			socialUrlType = "twitter.com/"
+			break
+
+		case ContactSocialType.FACEBOOK:
+			socialUrlType = "facebook.com/"
+			break
+
+		case ContactSocialType.XING:
+			socialUrlType = "xing.com/profile/"
+			break
+
+		case ContactSocialType.LINKED_IN:
+			socialUrlType = "linkedin.com/in/"
+			break
+	}
+
+	return `https://www.${socialUrlType}${socialId}`
+}
